body.text: Vidyākaraśānti: Tarkasopāna
body.translated_text: <s>Vidyākaraśānti</s>: <s>Tarkasopāna</s> (Staircase of Reasoning)

body.text: namo mañjuśriye //
body.translated_text: Homage to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>!

children.translated_text: Like a <s>kola</s> (jujube) fruit in the lake of <s>saṃsāra</s>, dispelling ignorance,
may the remembrance of <s>Hevajra</s> abide in my heart for a long time.

body.text: 1. hitāhitaprāptiparihārahetur niyamena pramāṇam iti saṃkṣepatas tad vyutpādyate // pramāṇam avisaṃvādi jñānam / visaṃvadanaṃ visaṃvādaḥ / na visaṃvādo 'visaṃvādaḥ / sa yasyāsti tad avisaṃvādi / saṃvādy evetyarthaḥ // avisaṃvādaḥ punar upadarśitā

children.translated_text: object's

children.text: pratibaddhārthakriyāprāpaṇam / prāpaṇam api prāpakatvaṃ tadyogyatā ca / avyavahitāyām arthakriyāyāṃ pramāṇasya prāpakatvam eva / vyavahitāyāṃ pravartakatvam api / prāpakatvaṃ copadarśakatvam eva / karaṇadharmasyopadarśakatvasya grahaṇād gṛhītagrahiṇām akaraṇatvena vyudāsān nātivyāpitā / ata evācāryo dharmottaro 'py āha // yenaiva prathamam upadarśitārthas tenaiva pravartitaḥ puruṣaḥ prāpitaś cārthaḥ kim anyenādhikaṃ kāryam / marīcikājalajñānādīny upadarśitārthapratibaddhārthakriyāprāpaṇāsaṃbhavād eva nirastānīti / jñānagrahaṇena cājñānasya indriyāder nirāsaḥ / karaṇavihitapratyayena ca gṛhītagrāhiṇaḥ / tena yad abhimatārthakriyāsamarthārthaprāpaṇayogyam apūrvaviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ tat pramāṇam //
children.translated_text: capacity to lead to the purpose (<s>arthakriyā</s>) connected with that [indicated object]. And 'leading to' also means 'having the capacity to lead,' that is, the suitability for it. With regard to a directly connected purpose, the <s>pramāṇa</s> has the capacity to lead; with regard to a remotely connected purpose, it also has the capacity to initiate action. And the capacity to lead is simply the capacity to indicate. Since [the definition] grasps the function of the instrument, namely the capacity to indicate, and since those who have already grasped [the object through another instrument] are excluded as being non-instruments, there is no over-extension. For this very reason, the master <s>Dharmottara</s> also says: 'The very thing by which an object is first indicated — by that very thing the person is set into action and the object is attained. What more is to be done by anything else?' Cognitions of mirages, water, and the like are excluded precisely because of the impossibility of leading to the purpose connected with the indicated object. And by the term 'knowledge' (<s>jñāna</s>), non-knowledge — sense organs and the like — is excluded. And by the term indicating an instrument, those who have already grasped [the object] are [excluded]. Therefore, that knowledge which is suitable for leading to the attainment of an object capable of fulfilling the desired purpose, and which has a novel object, is <s>pramāṇa</s>.

body.translated_text: 1. <s>Pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) is necessarily the means of obtaining what is beneficial and avoiding what is harmful — thus it is explained in brief. <s>Pramāṇa</s> is non-deceptive (<s>avisaṃvādi</s>) knowledge. Deception (<s>visaṃvadana</s>) is disagreement (<s>visaṃvāda</s>). The negation of disagreement is non-disagreement (<s>avisaṃvāda</s>). That which possesses it is non-deceptive — meaning: it is in agreement. Non-deception, moreover, is the indicated

body.text: 2. tad dvividham / pratyakṣam anumānaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: 2. That is of two kinds: <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference).

body.text: 3. pratigatam āśritam akṣaṃ pratyakṣam / atyādayaḥ krāntādyarthe dvitīyayeti samāsaḥ // prāptāpannālaṅgatisamāseṣu paraval liṅgapratiṣedhaḥ / tena pratyakṣaḥ pratyayaḥ pratyakṣā buddhiḥ / pratyakṣaṃ jñānam iti siddhaṃ bhavati / akṣāśritatvaṃ ca pratyakṣasya vyutpattimātranimittaṃ / pravṛttinimittaṃ tu sākṣātkaraṇam eva / tena yat kiṃcid viṣayasya sākṣātkāri jñānaṃ tat sarvaṃ pratyakṣaśabdavācyaṃ sidhyati / mīyate 'neneti mānam / liṅgagrahaṇasaṃbandhasmaraṇayoḥ paścānmānam anumānam / etac ca rūḍhivaśāl labhyate / tena dharmiviśeṣavarti liṅgaṃ dṛṣṭavato

children.translated_text: the mark

children.text: liṅginoś ca saṃbandhaṃ smṛtavato yataḥ parokṣavastvālambanaṃ jñānam utpadyate tad anumānaśabdenābhidhīyate //
children.translated_text: and who has recollected the connection between the mark and the mark-bearer — that is designated by the word <s>anumāna</s>.

body.translated_text: 3. That which has approached (<s>pratigata</s>) and depends upon (<s>āśrita</s>) a sense organ (<s>akṣa</s>) is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception). The prefix 'prati' and similar ones are used in the sense of 'having gone to' and so forth, with the second [case-ending] — thus is the compound. In the compounds with <s>prāpta</s>, <s>āpanna</s>, <s>alaṅgata</s>, and so forth, the gender follows the latter member. Hence: <s>pratyakṣaḥ pratyayaḥ</s> (a perceptual cognition, masculine), <s>pratyakṣā buddhiḥ</s> (a perceptual understanding, feminine), <s>pratyakṣaṃ jñānam</s> (a perceptual knowledge, neuter) — all are established. However, dependence on sense organs is merely the etymological basis of 'perception'; the functional basis is direct apprehension (<s>sākṣātkaraṇa</s>) alone. Therefore, whatever knowledge directly apprehends its object — all of that is denoted by the word <s>pratyakṣa</s>. That by which something is measured (<s>mīyate</s>) is a measure (<s>māna</s>). <s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is the measure that follows (<s>paścāt</s>) the apprehension of a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) and the recollection of the connection (<s>saṃbandha</s>). This is obtained by convention. Therefore, the knowledge that arises having a hidden object as its support — for one who has seen the logical mark existing in the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>),

body.text: 4. cakāraḥ pratyakṣānumānayos tulyabalatvaṃ samuccinoti / yathārthāvinābhāvitvāt pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇam / tathānumānam apy arthāvinābhāvi pramāṇam iti tad uktam //
body.translated_text: 4. The word 'ca' ('and') gathers together the equal strength (<s>tulyabalatva</s>) of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and <s>anumāna</s>. Just as <s>pratyakṣa</s> is a <s>pramāṇa</s> because it is not without the object, so too <s>anumāna</s>, being also not without the object, is a <s>pramāṇa</s>. As it is stated:

children.translated_text: 'In the absence of the object there is [no cognition and hence] no validity; even in the case of perception, validity [depends on this].
For that whose nature is invariably connected [with the object], being the cause of that — the two are equal.'

body.text: anenaiva tulyabalatvakhyāpanena yad api mīmāṃsakair uktaṃ sarvapramāṇānāṃ pratyakṣam eva jyeṣṭhaṃ tatpūrvakatvād anumānāder iti tad api nirastam // ātmasattālābhe sarvapramāṇānāṃ svakāraṇāpekṣatvān
body.translated_text: By this very declaration of equal strength, what was also stated by the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> — that among all <s>pramāṇas</s>, <s>pratyakṣa</s> alone is the foremost because <s>anumāna</s> and the rest presuppose it — is also refuted. Since for the acquisition of their own existence, all <s>pramāṇas</s> depend on their own causes,

body.text: na jyeṣṭhetarabhāvakalpanā sādhvīti / evaṃ pratyakṣānumānabhedena dviprakāram eva pramāṇaṃ //
body.translated_text: the imagining of a hierarchy of foremost and inferior is not valid. Thus, by the division into <s>pratyakṣa</s> and <s>anumāna</s>, <s>pramāṇa</s> is of exactly two kinds.

body.text: 5. dvividhavacanenaikaṃ pramāṇaṃ trīṇi catvāri pañca ṣad iti vipratipattayo nirasyante / tathāhi pratyakṣam eva pramāṇaṃ bārhaspatyānām / pratyakṣānumānāgamāḥ pramāṇāni āṃkhyānām / upamānam api naiyāyikānām / arthāpattir api prābhākarāṇām / abhāvo hi pratyakṣaṃ śabdaś ca pramāṇam iti vaiyākarāṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: 5. By saying 'two kinds,' the disputes regarding one, three, four, five, or six <s>pramāṇas</s> are refuted. For the <s>Bārhaspatyas</s> (followers of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>), <s>pratyakṣa</s> alone is a <s>pramāṇa</s>. For the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>, <s>pratyakṣa</s>, <s>anumāna</s>, and <s>āgama</s> (testimony) are <s>pramāṇas</s>. For the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, <s>upamāna</s> (analogy) is added. For the <s>Prābhākaras</s>, <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is also added. For the Grammarians (<s>Vaiyākaraṇas</s>), <s>abhāva</s> (absence), <s>pratyakṣa</s>, and <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony) are the <s>pramāṇas</s>.

body.text: 6. tatra pratyakṣaṃ kalpanāpodham abhrāntam / yaj jñā

children.translated_text: ledge

children.text: kalpanayā kalpanātvena rahitam abhrāntaṃ ca tad eva pratyakṣam / etena yad uktam udyotakareṇa / yadi pratyakṣaśabdena pratyakṣam abhidhīyate / kathaṃ tat kalpanāpoḍham / atha kalpanāpodhaṃ kathaṃ pratyakṣaṃ kalpanāpodham ity anena śabdenocyata iti / yad api bhartṛhariṇoktam / kalpanā hi jñānaṃ pratyakṣam api jñānaṃ / pratyakṣajñāne kalpanājñānaṃ pratiṣedhatānyasmin jnāne jñānāntaram astīti pratipāditam / prāptipūrvakā hi pratiṣedhā bhavantīti nyāyād iti / tat sarvam apāstam / tādātmyapratiṣedhasyātrābhimatatvāt / ata eva vivṛtaṃ kalpanayā kalpanātvena rahitam iti /
children.translated_text: is devoid of conceptualization in the manner of conceptualization, and is also non-erroneous — that alone is <s>pratyakṣa</s>. By this, what was said by <s>Udyotakara</s> — 'If the word <s>pratyakṣa</s> denotes perception, how can it be free from conceptualization? And if it is free from conceptualization, how can it be called "perception free from conceptualization" by this word?' — and also what was said by <s>Bhartṛhari</s> — 'Conceptualization is [a form of] knowledge, and perception is also [a form of] knowledge. When conceptual knowledge is negated in perceptual knowledge, it is taught that there is one knowledge within another knowledge. For negations presuppose [prior] attainment, according to logical principle.' — all of that is dismissed. Because what is intended here is the negation of essential identity (<s>tādātmya</s>). For this very reason it is explained: 'devoid of conceptualization in the manner of conceptualization.'

body.translated_text: 6. Therein, <s>pratyakṣa</s> is 'free from conceptualization' (<s>kalpanāpodha</s>) and 'non-erroneous' (<s>abhrānta</s>). Whatever know-

body.text: 7. kutaḥ punaḥ kalpanābhramayor abhāvaḥ pratyakṣa iti cet / yasmāt kalpanāvibhramayor artharūpasākṣātkaraṇaṃ nāsti / tathā hi / abhilāpasaṃsargayogyapratibhāsapratītiḥ kalpanā / abhilāpo vācakaḥ śabdaḥ / sa ca sāmānyākāraḥ / tena saṃsargyas tadyogyaḥ
body.translated_text: 7. But why are conceptualization and error absent in <s>pratyakṣa</s>? Because in conceptualization and in error there is no direct apprehension (<s>sākṣātkaraṇa</s>) of the nature of the object. For thus: <s>kalpanā</s> (conceptualization) is a cognition whose appearance (<s>pratibhāsa</s>) is suitable for association with verbal expression (<s>abhilāpasaṃsargayogya</s>). Verbal expression (<s>abhilāpa</s>) is the signifying word (<s>śabda</s>). And that has a universal form (<s>sāmānyākāra</s>). That which is fit to be conjoined with it — that appearance in a cognition which is suitable for association with expression — is [called] 'having an appearance suitable for association with expression.' By the word 'suitable' (<s>yogya</s>), the conceptualization of an infant who has not yet learned conventions is included.

body.text: pratibhāso yasyāṃ pratītau sā abhilāpasaṃsargayogyapratibhāsā / yogyagrahaṇenāvyutpannasaṃketasya bālakasya kalpanā saṃgṛhyate / yady api tasyām abhilāpasaṃsargo nāsti tadyogyā tu bhavaty eva / tatpratibhāsino 'rthākārasyecchādhīnasaṃketānuvidhāyinā śabdenābhidhātuṃ śakyatvāt / kutaḥ punar bālakasya kalpanā siddheti cet / tatkāryasya pravṛttyādilakṣaṇasya pradarśanāt // tathā hi bālako 'ṅguryādiparihāre stanādau pravartate / tad uktaṃ /
body.translated_text: For even though in that [infant's cognition] there is no actual association with verbal expression, there is indeed suitability for it — because the form of the object appearing therein can be designated by a word that follows convention dependent on will. But how is the infant's conceptualization established? By demonstrating its effect, characterized by purposeful activity and the like. For an infant, by the device of [pointing with] a finger and the like, engages with the breast and so forth. As it is stated:

children.translated_text: 'All purposeful activity in the world depends on words;
even an infant engages with it through previously implanted impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>).'

body.text: bālake punaḥ saṃmūrcchitākṣarākāradhvaniviśiṣṭā buddhiviparivartinī kalpanā ūhyā yayā paścāt saṃketagrahaṇakuśalo bhavati / na cedṛśīyam artharūpaṃ sākṣātkaroti / avyāpṛtendriyasya darśaṇavad buddhau śabdenāpratibhāsanād artha

children.translated_text: does not

children.text: sya / sa hi śabdasyārtho yaḥ śābde pratyaye pratibhāsate / upāyabhedāt prati
children.translated_text: appear to the mind through the word. For the meaning of a word is that which appears in the verbal cognition. The difference in cognition arises from the difference in means, not from the difference in the object. [Objection:] Just as the same <s>Devadatta</s> is seen through a door and through a lattice. [Reply:] This is not correct. Even when the means differ, since the very same form is grasped, how can there be a difference in cognition? And objects do not have two forms — one clear and one unclear — because that would be contradictory, and because the difference is grounded in this very [distinction]. For that very reason, the example is also unestablished. As it is stated:
cognition

children.text: bhedo nārthabhedāt / yathaika eva devadatto dvārād dṛśyate jālena ceti cet / ayuktam etat / upāyabhede 'pi tadrūpasyaiva grahaṇāt kathaṃ pratipattibhedaḥ / na ca vastūnāṃ dve rūpe spaṣṭāspaṣṭalakṣaṇe virodhād etannibandhanatvāc ca bhedasya / ata eva dṛṣṭānto 'py asiddhaḥ / tad uktam /
children.translated_text: [missing text due to line break]

body.translated_text: In the infant, however, one should infer a conceptualization that operates within the mind, characterized by confused letter-forms and sounds, by which he later becomes skilled in grasping conventions. Such [conceptualization] does not directly apprehend the nature of the object. Just as one whose sense organ is not engaged does not see, because the nature of the object

children.text: jāto nāmāśrayo nānyaś cetasāṃ tasya vastunaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The born [cognition] has no other substrate of that object by its name;
how could there be a form for one and the same thing that appears in different aspects?'

body.text: iti / tad evam abhilapituṃ śakyam evārthaṃ kalpanā
body.translated_text: Thus, conceptualization would grasp the object — which is indeed expressible —

body.text: śabdena saṃyojya gṛhṇīyāt / abhilāpyaṃ ca vastu sākṣātkriyamāṇaṃ śabdenāyojitam eva sākṣātkartavyam iti / siddham etat kalpanāyā nāsti vastusākṣātkaraṇam iti /
body.translated_text: by conjoining it with a word. But a real entity, when being directly apprehended, must be directly apprehended without being conjoined with a word. Thus it is established that conceptualization does not involve direct apprehension of the real entity.

body.text: 8.bhrāntam api jñānaṃ timirāśubhramaṇanauyānasaṃkṣobhādyāhitavibhramam artharūpavisaṃvādakam / tat katham anyathā sthitam arthaṃ sākṣātkuryāt / svarūpapratibhāsasya sākṣātkaraṇaśabdavācyatvāt / tasmān nāsti vastusākṣātkaraṇaṃ vibhramasyāpīti siddham / ataś ca vijñānaṃ viṣayasākṣātkāri niyamena kalpanāvibhramābhyāṃ viparītaṃ bhavat kalpanāpoḍham abhrāntaṃ cāvatiṣṭhate / tatra kalpanāpoḍhapadenānumānasya nirodhaḥ / abhrāntapadena dvicandrajñānādeḥ / anyārthaṃ kṛtam anyārthaṃ bhavatīti nyāyāt paravipratipattir api nirākṛtā draṣṭavyā / tathā hi vaiyākaraṇair uktam /
body.translated_text: 8. Erroneous cognition too — an error produced by cataracts, rapid eye movement, the rocking of a boat, and the like — is deceptive regarding the nature of the object. How could it directly apprehend an object that exists otherwise? Because the direct apprehension of one's own form-appearance is what is denoted by the word <s>sākṣātkaraṇa</s> (direct apprehension). Therefore, it is also established that error does not involve direct apprehension of the real entity. Hence, cognition that directly apprehends its object, necessarily being the opposite of both conceptualization and error, remains as 'free from conceptualization' (<s>kalpanāpodha</s>) and 'non-erroneous' (<s>abhrānta</s>). Here, by the term 'free from conceptualization,' <s>anumāna</s> (inference) is excluded. By the term 'non-erroneous,' cognitions of double moons and the like are excluded. By the principle that 'what is done for one purpose serves another purpose as well,' the opposing views of others are also to be seen as refuted. For the Grammarians (<s>Vaiyākaraṇas</s>) have stated:

children.text: na so 'sti pratyayo loke yaḥ śabdānugamād ṛte /
children.translated_text: 'There is no cognition in the world that arises without following words;

children.text: anuviddham iva jñānaṃ sarvaṃ śabdena jāyata //
children.translated_text: all knowledge arises as if pervaded by words.'

body.text: iti / sarvapratyayānāṃ śabdānugatarūpatve sati kasyacid api jñānasyārthasākṣātkaraṇayogāt / anubhavasiddhaṃ ca kalpanāpoḍhaṃ pratyakṣaṃ katham aṅkayate / aśvavikalpanakāle gor anubhavāt / tad evāvikalpakaṃ pratyakṣaṃ / na cāśvavikalpa eva gāṃ pratipadyate / svanāmopasaṃhitasya tasya tena grahaṇāt / na ca vikalpāntaraṃ dṛṣyaṃ saṃvedyate / etenāśvādivikalpakāle gavādivikalpo 'pi vyākhyātaḥ / tathā mīmāṃsakair api /
body.translated_text: Thus, since all cognitions have the form of being accompanied by words, how can any cognition have the capacity of directly apprehending the object? And how is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), which is established through experience as being free from conceptualization (<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>), [denied]? Because at the time of the conceptualization of a horse, there is the experience of a cow — that very [cognition] is non-conceptual <s>pratyakṣa</s>. And the conceptualization of a horse does not apprehend a cow, since that [cow-cognition], associated with its own name, is grasped by that [horse-conceptualization]. Nor is a different conceptualization perceived as an object of awareness. By this, the conceptualization of a cow and so forth at the time of the conceptualization of a horse and so forth is also explained. Likewise, by the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> (ritualist philosophers) also:

children.translated_text: 'There exists, indeed, a first non-conceptual cognition of apprehension (<s>ālocanā</s>),
resembling the cognition of infants and mutes, arising from a pure object.'

children.text: tataḥ paraṃ punar vastudharmair jātyādibhir yayā /
children.translated_text: 'After that, the cognition by which [the object] is determined through properties of the object such as genus (<s>jāti</s>) and so forth —
that too is accepted as having the nature of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception).' Thus —

body.text: anena vikalpasyāpi pratyakṣatvam iṣṭam / naiyāyikādibhir api vyavasāyātmakam ity ādinā niścayasyaiva pratyakṣatvam uktam etad api kalpanāpoḍham ity anenaiva nirastam / yadi kalpanātmakaṃ pratyakṣaṃ syād arthasākṣātkaritaiva hīyeta iti//
body.translated_text: by this, even conceptualization is accepted as <s>pratyakṣa</s>. By the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> (logicians) and others too, through [the definition beginning with] 'having the nature of determinate cognition (<s>vyavasāyātmaka</s>),' the <s>pratyakṣa</s> nature of ascertainment alone has been stated — but this too is refuted by the very [phrase] 'free from conceptualization (<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>).' If <s>pratyakṣa</s> were of the nature of conceptualization, then the very direct apprehension of the object would be lost.

body.text: 9. abhrāntagrahaṇenāpi śuklaśaṅkhādau pītaśaṅkhādivijñānaṃ nirasyate / saty api bhrame 'rthakriyāvisaṃvādābhāvāt / nāpi tad anumānaṃ yujyate liṅgajatvāt / ataḥ pratyakṣam iti / kathaṃ punar etad abhrāntagrahaṇenāvisaṃvādārthena nirasyate / ucyate / adhyavasitārthākārapratirūpārthakriyāprāpter asaṃbhavāt / yadi hy avisaṃvāditāmātreṇa pramāṇaṃ syāt keśoṇḍukādijñāne 'pi ālokādeḥ saṃvādasaṃbhavāt tad api pramāṇaṃ syāt //
body.translated_text: 9. By the qualification 'non-erroneous' (<s>abhrānta</s>), the cognition of a yellow conch-shell and so forth [when the conch is actually] white is also excluded — because despite the error, there is no discordance with practical efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>). Nor is that rightly [classified as] inference (<s>anumāna</s>), since it arises from a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>). Therefore, it is <s>pratyakṣa</s>. But how is this excluded by the qualification 'non-erroneous,' whose meaning is 'non-discordant'? It is said: because it is impossible to achieve practical efficacy conforming to the form of the object as determined. For if something were a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) merely by non-discordance, then even the cognition of floating hairs and so forth would also be a <s>pramāṇa</s>, since concordance with light and so forth is possible [even there].

body.text: 10. tat pratyakṣaṃ caturvidhaṃ / indriyajñānaṃ mānasaṃ svasaṃvedanaṃ yogijñānaṃ ceti //
body.translated_text: 10. That <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) is fourfold: sense-cognition (<s>indriyajñāna</s>), mental [perception] (<s>mānasa</s>), self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>), and yogic cognition (<s>yogijñāna</s>).

That which is generated by sense-cognition together with a homogeneous moment apprehending the moment immediately following its own object-moment, as an immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>), and which has mere mind as its support, is mental perception (<s>mānasa</s>). Their cognition, which arises from

body.text: 12. tathā hi vaibhāṣikais tāvaj jñānasyāpratighatvād yadi tad draṣṭṛ syād tadā vyavahitam api gṛhṇīyād itīndriyaṃ draṣṭṛ kalpitaṃ / na caitad yuktam / yadi hi jñānaṃ gatvārthaṃ gṛhṇāti tadā gamanavibandhakābhāvād vyavahitam api gṛhṇīyād iti yujyate vaktum / kiṃ tu / yadākāraṃ taj jñānam utpadyate tat tena gṛhītam ity ucyate na cāyogyadeśastho 'rthas tatsarūpakaḥ / tat kathaṃ tasya tena grahaṇaṃ syāt / kiṃ ca / yadīndriyaṃ draṣṭṛ syāt tadā kācādivyavahitasyārthasya grahaṇaṃ na syāt / sapratighā daśa rūpiṇa iti siddhāntāt / katham āgame uktam / cakṣuṣā gṛhyate rūpam iti / aupacāriko 'sau nirdeśaḥ //
body.translated_text: 12. For the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> (Sarvāstivādin realists), since cognition is non-resistant (<s>apratigha</s>), if it were the perceiver, then it would apprehend even what is obstructed — thus they conceive the sense faculty as the perceiver. But this is not correct. For if cognition grasps the object by going [to it], then since there is no obstacle to movement, it is reasonable to say it would also grasp what is obstructed. However, that cognition which arises bearing the form [of the object] — that is said to be 'grasped by it'; and an object situated in an unsuitable location does not conform to its image. So how could it be grasped by that [cognition]? Moreover, if the sense faculty were the perceiver, then there would be no perception of an object obstructed by glass and the like — since 'the ten material [faculties] have resistance' is an established doctrinal principle. How then is it stated in scripture: 'Form is grasped by the eye'? That statement is figurative.

body.text: 13. yad api kumārilādibhir uktam / yadīndriyajñānagṛhītam arthaṃ gṛhṇāti mānasam / tadā gṛhītagrāhitvād asyāprāmāṇyam / athendriyajñānāgṛhītam arthaṃ gṛhṇāti / tadā cāndhabadhirādyabhāvadoṣaprasaṅga iti / tad api svaviṣayakṣaṇopādeyasajātīyakṣaṇasahitenendriyajñānena yaj janitam ity anenaiva nirastam / tathā hīndriyajñānaviṣayopādeyabhūtakṣaṇagrāhi mānasam / na ca indriyajñānam andhādīnām asti / tat kuto 'ndhabadhirādyahhāvadoṣaḥ / nāpi
body.translated_text: 13. As for what has been said by <s>Kumārila</s> and others: 'If mental [perception] grasps the object grasped by sense-cognition, then since it grasps what is already grasped, it would lack validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>). But if it grasps an object not grasped by sense-cognition, then the absurd consequence would be the absence of blindness, deafness, and so forth' — this too is refuted by the very [phrase] 'that which is generated by sense-cognition together with a homogeneous moment apprehending the moment immediately following its own object-moment.' For mental [perception] grasps the moment that is the immediate successor to the object-moment of sense-cognition. And the blind and others do not have sense-cognition; so how could there be the defect of absence of blindness, deafness, and so forth? Nor is there

body.text: gṛhītagrāhitā / indriyajñānaviṣayopādeyabhūtakṣaṇasyānena grahaṇāt / etac ca mānasaṃ pratyakṣam uparatavyāpāre cakṣurādau pratyakṣam iṣyate / vyāpriyamāṇe punar etasmin yat pratyakṣaṃ tac ced anindriyajaṃ kim anyad indriyajaṃ bhaviṣyati / na ca nimīlitākṣasya rūpadarśanābhāvād anubhavaviruddhatvam āśaṅkanīyam / kṣaṇamātrabhāvitvena duravadhāratvāt //
body.translated_text: the grasping of what is already grasped, since what is grasped [by mental perception] is the moment that is the immediate successor to the object-moment of sense-cognition. And this mental <s>pratyakṣa</s> is accepted as <s>pratyakṣa</s> when the operation of the eye and other [sense faculties] has ceased. But if, while they are still operating, there is a <s>pratyakṣa</s> that is not born from the sense faculties — what else would be born from the sense faculties? Nor should one suspect that this contradicts experience because one whose eyes are closed does not see forms — since, being momentary in duration, it is difficult to ascertain.

children.translated_text: by opponents regarding <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caittas</s> (mental factors) — that too is unreasonable. For it is not the case that the luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>) of <s>citta</s> and <s>caittas</s> simply does not exist, since luminosity is established through the experience of all sentient beings. Nor is it reasonable that they are illuminated by something other [than themselves]. For that other [illuminator], being contemporaneous, cannot be an illuminator — due to the absence of any beneficial function. And a temporally different [illuminator] too cannot be an illuminator — due to the absence of the thing to be illuminated. Therefore, just as a lamp, being of the nature of illumination, illuminates itself, so too does cognition. If one objects: 'But a lamp too is illuminated by the eye!' — [the answer is:] No, because it is used as an example precisely because it does not depend on a homogeneous illumination.

Therein, that which

'Presence' of the object of cognition means its being in a suitable place. 'Absence' means its complete non-existence in a suitable place. That which, by these two [presence and absence], differentiates the cognitive appearance — the graspable aspect — through its arising or non-arising, that is the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>. What is other is the <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s> (universal characteristic) — that is the object of <s>anumāna</s> (inference). What is other than this <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, the common characteristic, is the object of inference.

By this, the attribution of having a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) as its object is refuted regarding <s>pratyakṣa</s>. The presence or absence of the object

body.text: 19. tad eva pratyakṣaṃ jñānaṃ pramāṇaphalam / arthapratītirūpatvāt yad evānantaram uktaṃ pratyakṣaṃjñānaṃtad eva pramāṇasya phalam / arthasya pratītir avagamaḥ / tadrūpatvāt / yadi tad eva jñānaṃ pramāṇaphalaṃ neṣyate tadā bhinnaviṣayatvaṃ syāt pramāṇaphalayoḥ / na caitad yuktam / na hi paraśvādike khadiraprāpte palāśe cchidā bhavati //
body.translated_text: 19. That very perceptual cognition is the fruit of the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition). Because it has the nature of the apprehension of the object — the very perceptual cognition just described is the fruit of the <s>pramāṇa</s>. The apprehension (<s>pratīti</s>) of the object means its cognition. Because it has that nature. If that very cognition were not accepted as the fruit of the <s>pramāṇa</s>, then there would be a difference of object between the <s>pramāṇa</s> and its fruit. And this is not proper. For there is no cutting of a <s>palāśa</s> (tree) when a <s>khadira</s> is reached, as in the case of another's dog and so forth.

body.text: 20. arthasārūpyam asya pramāṇam / tadvaśād arthapratītisiddheḥ / iha yasmād viṣayād vijñānam udeti tatsarūpaṃ tad bhavati / atatsarūpeṇa jñānenārthavedanāyogāt / tathā hi vijñānaṃ bodhamātrasvabhāvam
body.translated_text: 20. The resemblance to the object (<s>arthasārūpya</s>) is its <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of validity). Because the apprehension of the object is established by virtue of that [resemblance]. Here, from whichever object a cognition arises, it becomes similar in form to that [object]. Because by a cognition that is not similar in form to that [object], the experience of the object would not be possible. For cognition, which has the nature of mere awareness,

body.text: utpadyate / tadā nīlasyedaṃ vedanaṃ pītasyeti pratikarmavyavasthā na syāt / yādṛśaṃ hi tan nile pīte 'pi tādṛśaṃ ceti / arthasārūpye tu sati yasyaivākāram anukaroti jñānaṃ tatsaṃvedanaṃ bhavati nānyasya / tac cāsya sārūpyaṃ niyatārthapratītivyavasthāyāṃ sādhakatamatvāt pramāṇam / na caitat mantavyam / kathaṃ sādhyasādhanayor abheda iti / janyajanakabhāvenātra sādhyasādhanabhāvābhāvāt / vyavasthāpyavyavasthāpakabhāvena caikasyāpi ghaṭate / nāpi lokabādhā / loko pi kadācid ekadhanurādikaṃ kartṛtvādinā vadaty eva / tathāhi vaktāro bhavanti / dhanur vidhyati / dhanuṣā vidhyati / dhanuṣo nisṛtya saro vidhyatīti / etena pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ jñānaṃ pramāṇam uttaram uttaraṃ phalam iti pramāṇaphalabhrāntir apāstā // //
body.translated_text: arises [as such]. Then the determination 'this is the experience of blue, this of yellow' — the allocation to each action — would not be possible. For whatever it is like with respect to blue, it would be the same with yellow. But when there is resemblance to the object, the cognition that imitates the form of precisely that [object] becomes the experience of that and not of another. And this resemblance, being most effective in establishing the fixed determination of the object, is the <s>pramāṇa</s>. Nor should one think: 'How can there be non-difference between what is to be established and the means of establishing it?' Because here the relationship of what is to be established and the means of establishing has no reality in terms of the effect-cause relationship. And even for a single entity, the relationship of what is to be determined and the means of determining is possible. Nor is there contradiction with ordinary convention. Ordinary people too sometimes speak of a single bow and so forth in terms of agency, etc. For speakers say: 'The bow pierces,' 'he pierces with the bow,' 'the arrow, released from the bow, pierces.' By this, the confusion regarding <s>pramāṇa</s> and fruit — that the earlier cognition is the <s>pramāṇa</s> and the later one the fruit — is removed.

body.text: 1. anumānaṃ dvidhā svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca / svasmāyidaṃ svārthaṃ / yena svayaṃ pratipadyate / parasmāyidaṃ parārtham / yena paraṃ pratipādayati /
body.translated_text: 1. <s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is twofold: <s>svārtha</s> (for oneself) and <s>parārtha</s> (for others). That which is for oneself is <s>svārtha</s> — by which one understands for oneself. That which is for another is <s>parārtha</s> — by which one makes another understand.

body.text: 2. tatra trirūpaliṅgād yad anumeye jñānaṃ rūpatrayayuktāl liṅgād yad anumeyālambanaṃ jñānaṃ utpadyate tat svārtham anumānam / trirūpagrahaṇam ekaikadvidvirūpavyavacchedārtham / tatraikaikarūpo hetur na bhavati / yathā nityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvāt / mūrtatvāt / aprameyatvād iti / yathākramam anumeye sattvasapakṣasattvavipakṣa
body.translated_text: 2. Therein, the cognition that arises from the <s>liṅga</s> (logical mark) possessing the three characteristics, regarding the object to be inferred — the cognition whose object is the <s>anumeya</s> (object to be inferred), arising from the logical mark endowed with the three forms — that is <s>svārthānumāna</s> (inference for oneself). The mention of 'three forms' is for the purpose of excluding [marks with] only one, only two forms. Therein, a <s>hetu</s> (reason) with only one form is not [valid]. For example: 'Sound is eternal, because it is produced' [has existence in the subject]; 'because it is corporeal' [has existence in the similar case]; 'because it is immeasurable' [has existence in the dissimilar case]. In order, there is merely existence in the <s>anumeya</s>, existence in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar case), and exclusion from the <s>vipakṣa</s> (dissimilar case).

body.translated_text: Here too, by the mention of 'existence,' the contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>) is excluded. For example: 'eternal, because of being produced.' For that exists not only in the <s>sapakṣa</s> but in both [similar and dissimilar cases]. By the determination-word before the 'existence'-word, the status as a reason of one whose presence pervades only part of the <s>sapakṣa</s> is also stated. For example: 'eternal, because of being produced immediately after effort.' By the repeated mention of 'ascertained,' the inconclusive with doubtful positive concomitance is excluded. For example: 'Someone is omniscient, because of being a speaker.' The <s>asapakṣa</s> (dissimilar case) is of the forthcoming definition. Its non-existence alone, ascertained — that is the third form. Therein, by the mention of 'non-existence,' the contradictory is excluded. For the contradictory exists in the <s>vipakṣa</s>. body.text: 7. na sapakṣo 'sapakṣaḥ [ tato 'nyas tadviruddhas tadabhāvaś ca / trirūpāṇi ca trīṇy eva liṅgāṇi / anupalabdhiḥ svabhāvaḥ kāryaṃ ceti / tatra pratiṣedhyasyopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdhir abhāvavyavahārasādhanī / upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptir upalambhapratyayāntarasākalyam /
body.translated_text: 7. The <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar instance) is not the <s>asapakṣa</s> (dissimilar instance), [and the latter is] what is other than that, what is contrary to that, and the absence of that. And the three characteristics are three logical marks only: <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension), <s>svabhāva</s> (essential nature), and <s>kārya</s> (effect). Among these, the non-apprehension of what is to be negated, when it has fulfilled the conditions for being apprehended, establishes the convention of absence. The fulfillment of the conditions for apprehension means the completeness of the other conditions for apprehension.

body.text: svabhāvaviśeṣaś ca / yaḥ svabhāvaḥ satsv anyeṣūpalambhapratyayeṣu san pratyakṣa eva bhavati / upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpto 'rthaḥ / dṛśya ity arthaḥ / avidyamāno 'py asāv atra yadi bhaved dṛśya eva bhaved iti saṃbhavanaviṣaya upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta ity ucyate / tasyānupalabdhir abhāvavyavahāraṃ sādhayati / deśakālasvabhāvaviprakṛṣṭapratyayāntaravikalavyavacchedārthaṃ viśeṣaṇopādānam / na cātra pratiṣedhamātram anupalabdhiḥ tasya svayam asiddheḥ siddheś cānaṅgatvāt / kiṃ tu vastvantarasyopalabdhir eva / vastuno 'pi na yasya kasyacit / api tu pratiṣedhyābhāvākṣepakasyaiva / na tv ekajñānasaṃsargina eva / yadi hy ekajñānasaṃsargivastvantaropalambho 'nupalabdher lakṣaṇaṃ syāt tadā iha devadattopalambhād bahirabhāvas tasyaiva kathaṃ sidhyati / na hi tatraikajñānasaṃsargivastvantaropalambho 'sti //
body.translated_text: And the specific nature: that nature which, when the other conditions for apprehension are present, would be directly perceptible — that is an object that has fulfilled the conditions for apprehension. The meaning is: 'visible.' Even if non-existent here, if it were to exist, it would be visible indeed — in this sense, as a possible object, it is called 'having fulfilled the conditions for apprehension.' Its non-apprehension establishes the convention of absence. The qualification is adopted for the purpose of excluding what is remote in place, time, own-nature, and deficient in other conditions. And here, <s>anupalabdhi</s> is not mere negation, since that is itself unestablished, and even if established, it would be irrelevant. Rather, it is the apprehension of some other entity. But not just any entity whatsoever. Rather, only of an entity that implies the absence of what is to be negated. But not necessarily one that is in contact with a single cognition. For if the apprehension of another entity in contact with a single cognition were the definition of non-apprehension, then how could the external absence of <s>Devadatta</s> himself be established from the apprehension of <s>Devadatta</s>? For there is no apprehension of another entity in contact with a single cognition there.

But when it is a property of the agent, then it refers to the cognition based on that. Regarding this, that absence of the pot is the very nature of the ground itself, and is thus already grasped by the cognition that grasps that [ground]. Therefore, this non-apprehension establishes the convention of absence only for the confused. For the non-confused, it is already established through direct perception. And this [non-apprehension] in the present tense is effective; in the past tense also, when there is no lapse of memory or attention. Therefore, 'there is no pot here, because it is not apprehended'; 'there was no pot here, because it was not apprehended' —

For the nature of the cold touch to be negated has fire as its contrary, and its apprehension here [is the proof]. 6) Apprehension of what is contrary to the cause (<s>kāraṇaviruddhopalabdhi</s>): For example, 'There are no horripilation and similar effects here, because of the proximity of a particular fire.' For the cause of the horripilation and similar effects to be negated is cold, and the particular fire is contrary to that, and its apprehension here [is the proof]. 7) Apprehension of what is contrary to the pervader (<s>vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhi</s>): For example, 'There is no frost-touch here, because of fire.' For the pervader of the frost-touch to be negated is cold, and fire is contrary to that, and its apprehension here [is the proof]. 8) Apprehension of what is contrary to the effect (<s>kāryaviruddhopalabdhi</s>): For example, 'The causes of cold with unobstructed capacity are not present here, because of fire.' For the effect of the causes of cold to be negated is cold, and fire is contrary to that, and its apprehension here [is the proof].

14) kāraṇaviruddhakāryopalabdhir yathā na romaharṣādiviśeṣayuktapuruṣavān ayaṃ pradeśo dhūmād iti / pratiṣedhyānāṃ romaharṣādiviśeṣānāṃ kāraṇaṃ śītaṃ tasya viruddho 'gnis tasya kāryaṃ dhūmas tasya cehopabdhiḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>opalabdhi</s>): For example, 'This is not permanent, because of being an occasional cause.' For the pervader of the permanence to be negated is unsurpassability, and its contrary is surpassability, and being an occasional cause is pervaded by that, and its apprehension here [is the proof]. 12) Apprehension of what is pervaded by the contrary of the effect (<s>kāryaviruddhavyāptopalabdhi</s>): For example, 'The causes of fire with unobstructed capacity are not present here, because of frost-touch.' For the effect of the causes of fire to be negated is fire, and cold is contrary to that, and frost-touch is pervaded by that, and its apprehension here [is the proof]. 13) Apprehension of the effect of what is contrary to the own-nature (<s>svabhāvaviruddhakāryopalabdhi</s>): For example, 'There is no cold touch here, because of smoke.' For the contrary of the cold touch to be negated is fire, and smoke is its effect, and its apprehension here [is the proof]. 14) Apprehension of the effect of what is contrary to the cause (<s>kāraṇaviruddhakāryopalabdhi</s>): For example, 'This place does not contain a person with horripilation and similar effects, because of smoke.' For the cause of the horripilation and similar effects to be negated is cold, and fire is contrary to that, and smoke is its effect, and its apprehension here [is the proof].

For the pervader of the frost-touch to be negated is cold, and fire is contrary to that, and smoke is its effect, and its apprehension here [is the proof]. 16) Apprehension of the effect of what is contrary to the effect (<s>kāryaviruddhakāryopalabdhi</s>): For example, 'The causes of cold with unobstructed capacity are not present here, because of smoke.' For the effect of the causes of cold to be negated is cold, and fire is contrary to that, and smoke is its effect, and its apprehension here [is the proof].

body.text: 10. ime sarve kāraṇānupalabdhyādayaḥ pañcadaśānupalabdhiprayogāḥ svabhāvānupalabdhau saṃgraham upayānti pāraṃparyeṇārthāntaravidhipratiṣedhābhyāṃ prayogahhede 'pi svabhāvānupalabdhau saṃgrahaṃ tādātmyena gacchanti / etad uktaṃ bhavati / anupalabdhirūpatā tāvat sarvāsām aviśiṣṭā / tathā svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhyādāv apy anupalabdhirūpatā vidyata eva / sahābhāvākṣepikā yasyopalabdhiḥ sā tasyānupalabdhir ity anupalabdhilakṣaṇayogāt / tathā hi yeyaṃ vahner upalabdhiḥ sā śītābhāvam ākṣipati /
body.translated_text: 10. All these fifteen applications of non-apprehension — from non-apprehension of the cause onward — are subsumed under non-apprehension of own-nature indirectly, through positive assertion and negation of other things; even with differences in application, they are subsumed under non-apprehension of own-nature through identity. This is what is being said: The character of being non-apprehension is undifferentiated for all [types]. Likewise, even in the apprehension of what is contrary to the own-nature and so forth, the character of non-apprehension exists. The apprehension of that which implies the co-absence [of another] is the non-apprehension of that [other] — because of satisfying the definition of non-apprehension. For instance, the apprehension of fire implies the absence of cold.

body.text: 11. bhavatv anupalabdhiḥ sā dṛśyatā tu katham / ucyate / dṛśyatve 'py anupalabdhir iti kṛtvā / tathā hi yadi śītasparśo dṛśyo bhavet tadā tasyopalabdhiṃ niṣedhyābhāvavyāpto vahnir viruṇaddhy eva / evam abhāvasādhanī sarvaivānupalabdhir vyāptisāmarthyād
body.translated_text: 11. Let it be non-apprehension; but how is visibility [established]? It is said: Because even in the case of visibility, it is non-apprehension. For if the cold touch were visible, then fire, which pervades the absence of what is to be negated, would indeed obstruct its apprehension. Thus all non-apprehension that establishes absence, by the force of the invariable concomitance,

body.text: dṛśyasyopalabdhiṃ viruṇaddhīti sāmarthyāt svabhāvānupalabdhir bhavati / na sākṣāt / yasyāṃ tv anupalabdhau tadaiva tam eva pratipattāraṃ prati dṛśyatvaṃ pratiṣedhyasya siddhaṃ dṛśyānupalabdhir eva tasyāḥ svalakṣaṇam iti sākṣāt svabhāvānupalabdhiḥ / yat punar anyair ucyate / yady api saṃpratitanī dṛśyānupalabdhir nāsti virodhādikāle tv āsīd saiva bhāvapratipattinibandhanam iti / tena dṛṣyānupalabdhipūrvatvāt svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhyādīnāṃ dṛśyānupalabdhāv antarbhāvaḥ / saṃpratitanyaś ca dṛśyānupalabdher abhāvāt tatsvabhāvānupalabdher anyāsām anupalabdhīnāṃ bheda iti /
body.translated_text: obstructs the apprehension of the visible — therefore by its capacity it is non-apprehension of own-nature. Not directly. But in that non-apprehension where the visibility of what is to be negated is established for that very cognizer at that very time — non-apprehension of the visible is its essential characteristic — that is directly non-apprehension of own-nature. Now, what others say: 'Even though present non-apprehension of the visible does not exist [in cases of contrary apprehension], it did exist at the time of contrariety and such, and that very [prior non-apprehension] is the basis for the cognition of [the thing's] existence.' Therefore, because non-apprehension of what is contrary to own-nature and so forth are preceded by non-apprehension of the visible, they are subsumed under non-apprehension of the visible. And since presently there is no non-apprehension of the visible, the other non-apprehensions are different from non-apprehension of own-nature.

body.text: 12. yad api kaiścit svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhyādīnām anumitānumānatayā dṛśyānupalabdhirūpatocyate / dūrād vahne rūpaviśeṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā uṣṇasparśaviśeṣas taddeśavyāpako 'numīyate tasmāc ca śītasparśābhāvapratītiḥ / āhatya tu dṛśyānupalabdher anudayād dṛśyānupalabdher bhedena nirdeśaḥ / ata eva cānumitānumānam etat kevalam atyantābhyāsāj jhaṭiti tathābhūtapratītyudaye saty ekam anumānam ucyate / vastutas tv anekam anumānam etat evam anyatrāpi vyāpakaviruddhopalambhādāv ūhyam iti dvayam apy etan na manasi toṣam ādadhāti //
body.translated_text: 12. Even though some describe the non-apprehension of the perceptible as being in the form of inferred inference (<s>anumitānumāna</s>)—such as in the apprehension of a contradictory nature (<s>svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhi</s>)—[they say:] upon seeing from a distance a particular color of fire, a particular heat-touch pervading that place is inferred, and from that the non-existence of cold-touch is cognized. But since non-apprehension of the perceptible does not arise in its entirety, the separate specification of non-apprehension of the perceptible is made. For this very reason, this is merely inferred inference; however, due to extreme habituation, when such a cognition arises instantaneously, it is called a single inference. In reality, however, this is multiple inference. The same should be understood in other cases such as the apprehension of what contradicts the pervader (<s>vyāpakaviruddhopalambha</s>). Thus, neither of these two [explanations] satisfies the mind.

body.text: 13. svabhāvaḥ svasattāmātrabhāvini sādhyadharme hetuḥ / yo hetor ātmanaḥ sattām apekṣya vidyamāno na hetusattāvyatiriktaṃ kiṃcid dhetum apekṣate / tasmin sādhye yo hetuḥsa svabhāvaḥ / anena ca viśeṣaṇe nāntyāt kāraṇāt kāryaṃ yad utpadyate tasya saṃgrahaḥ
body.translated_text: 13. <s>Svabhāva</s> (essential nature) is the logical reason (<s>hetu</s>) when the property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharma</s>) exists merely by virtue of the existence of [the reason] itself. That which, depending on the existence of the reason itself, does not require any other cause beyond the existence of the reason—when the property to be proved is such, the logical reason is called <s>svabhāva</s>. And by this qualification, the inclusion is made

For that too is indeed the essential nature of that [cause], since it exists merely by virtue of the existence of that [cause]. For example: 'This is a tree, because it is a <s>śiṃśapā</s>.' The effect is invariably concomitant with the cause through however many essential natures—this is the topic at hand. When the cause is what is to be proved, the logical reason consists of exactly those essential natures with which it is invariably concomitant. For example: 'There is fire here, because of smoke.'

body.text: 14. etāni ca trīṇi liṅgāni sādhyabhedāt / sādhyāpekṣayā hi liṅgavyavasthā / sādhyaś ca vidhiḥ pratiṣedho vā anyonyalakṣaṇavyavacchedalakṣaṇatvād anayoḥ / vidhir apy anarthāntarārthāntarabhedād dvividhaḥ / tatrānarthāntare gamye svabhāvahetuḥ / arthāntare tu gamye kāryam iti dvāv etau vidhisādhanau / svabhāvapratibandhe hi saty artho 'rthaṃ gamayet / svabhāvena pratibandhaḥ pratibaddhasvabhāvatvam / yasmāt svabhāvapratibandhe sati sādhanārthaḥ sādhyārthaṃ gamayet / tasmād anayor eva vidhisādhanatā / nanu svabhāvapratibandham antareṇāpi candrodayāt kumudavikāsapratipattiḥ samudravṛddhiś ca / ātapasadbhāvāt parabhāge chāyāpratipattiḥ / kṛttikādyudayānantaraś ca rohiṇyādīnām udayaḥ pratīyate / tat katham ucyate svabhāvapratibandhe saty artho 'rthaṃ gamayed iti / tadapratibaddhasya tadavyabhicāraniyamābhāvāt / tad iti
body.translated_text: 14. These three types of logical marks are distinguished according to the difference in what is to be proved. For the classification of the logical mark depends on what is to be proved. And what is to be proved is either an affirmation (<s>vidhi</s>) or a negation (<s>pratiṣedha</s>), since these two are defined by the mutual exclusion of each other's characteristics. Affirmation too is twofold, due to the distinction between what is not a different entity and what is a different entity. Therein, when what is to be cognized is not a different entity, the logical reason is <s>svabhāva</s>; when what is to be cognized is a different entity, it is <s>kārya</s> (effect)—thus these two are proofs of affirmation. For when there is an essential connection (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>), one thing can make another known. Essential connection means having a bound essential nature. Since the probans makes the probandum known when there is essential connection, therefore only these two serve as proofs of affirmation. [Objection:] But even without essential connection, one cognizes the blooming of night-lotuses from the rising of the moon, and the swelling of the ocean. From the presence of sunshine, one cognizes shadow on the far side. After the rising of <s>Kṛttikā</s> and other stars, the rising of <s>Rohiṇī</s> and others is cognized. How then can it be said that one thing makes another known only when there is essential connection? [Reply:] Because, for what is not essentially bound to that, there is no invariable non-deviation from that. 'That'

And the very particular wind that is the cause of the rising of <s>Kṛttikā</s> and others is, through its continuum, the cause of the rising of <s>Rohiṇī</s> and others. Since the cognition of the property of the logical reason leads to that cognition, it is the same here too. Wherever there is non-deviation, essential connection should be inferred. And that essential connection is of the logical mark with respect to the property to be proved—in reality, through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) with that and through arising from that (<s>tadutpatti</s>). Since what is not of that essential nature and does not arise from that has an essential nature not bound to it, and since identity and arising-from-that belong only to essential nature and effect respectively, establishment of reality is through these two alone. The establishment of negation, however, is through non-apprehension as described. [Objection:] But what essential connection is there in non-apprehension? And an essentially connected reason is what makes [the probandum] known. For it was just now stated:

body.text: 1. trirūpaliṅgākhyānaṃ parārtham anumānam / pūrvam uktaṃ yat trirūpaṃ liṅgaṃ tasya yat prakāśakaṃ vacanaṃ tat parārtham anumānaṃ kāraṇe kāryopacārāt / anumānakāraṇe trirūpaiiṅge kāryasyānumānasyopacārāt samāropāt / yathā naḍvalodakaṃ pādaroga iti / tad dvividhaṃ prayogabhedāt / sādharmyavat / vaidharmyavac ca //
body.translated_text: 1. The declaration of the three-featured logical mark (<s>trirūpaliṅga</s>) constitutes inference for others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>). The statement (<s>vacana</s>) that illuminates the three-featured logical mark previously described is inference for others, through the figurative application of the term for the effect to the cause. That is, through figurative attribution (<s>upacāra</s>) of the effect (inference) to its cause (the three-featured mark). Just as 'river water cures foot disease.' This is twofold, due to the distinction in formulation: by agreement (<s>sādharmyavat</s>) and by disagreement (<s>vaidharmyavat</s>).

body.text: 2. samāno dharmo yasya sa sadharmā / tasya bhāvaḥ sādharmyaṃ / dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇā saha sādhyadharmiṇo hetukṛtaṃ sādṛśyam / visadṛśo dharmo yasya sa vidharmā tasya bhāvo vaidharmyam / dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇā saha sādhyadharmiṇo hetukṛtaṃ vaisādṛśyam / yasya sādhanavākyasya sādharmyam abhidheyaṃ tatsādharmyavat / yasya ca vaidharmyam abhidheyaṃ tad vaidharmyavat / nanu ca sādharmyavati sādhanavākye vyatireko nāsti / vaidharmyavati cānvayas tat kathaṃ trirūpaliṅgākhyānaṃ parārtham anumānaṃ syāt / naiṣa doṣaḥ / sādharmyeṇāpi hi prayoge 'rthād vaidharmyagatiḥ / asati tasmin sādhyena hetor anvayāyogāt / sādharmyābhidheyena yukte prayoge samarthyād vyatirekasya pratītis tasmāt trirūpaliṅgākhyānam / tasmin vyatireke buddhyāvasīyamāne 'sati sādhyena hetor anvayasya buddhyāvasitasyābhāvāt //
body.translated_text: 2. That which has a similar property is <s>sadharmā</s> (agreeing). Its state is <s>sādharmya</s> (agreement)—the similarity, produced by the logical reason, of the subject (<s>sādhyadharmin</s>) with the example (<s>dṛṣṭāntadharmin</s>). That which has a dissimilar property is <s>vidharmā</s> (disagreeing). Its state is <s>vaidharmya</s> (disagreement)—the dissimilarity, produced by the logical reason, of the subject with the example. A probative statement whose content is agreement is called <s>sādharmyavat</s>. One whose content is disagreement is called <s>vaidharmyavat</s>. [Objection:] But in the probative statement by agreement, there is no negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>); and in that by disagreement, there is no positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>). How then can the declaration of the three-featured mark be inference for others? [Reply:] This is no fault. For even in formulation by agreement, the understanding of disagreement follows by implication (<s>arthāt</s>), since without it the positive concomitance of the reason with the probandum would not be possible. In a formulation expressed through agreement, the understanding of negative concomitance arises through implication; therefore it is a declaration of the three-featured mark. For without that negative concomitance being apprehended by the intellect, the positive concomitance of the reason with the probandum, as apprehended by the intellect, would not exist.

body.text: 3. tathā vaidharmyeṇāpy anvayagatiḥ / asati tasmin sādhyābhave hetvabhāvasyāsiddheḥ / tatheti yathānvayavākye tathārthād eva vaidharmyeṇa prayoge 'nvayasyānabhidhīyamānasyāpi gatiḥ / asati tasminn anvaye buddhigṛhīte sādhyābhāve hetvabhāvasyāsiddher anavasāyāt / tasmād ekenāpi vākyenānvayamukhena vyatirekamukhena vā prayuktena sapakṣāsapakṣayor liṅgasya sadasattvakhyāpanaṃ kṛtaṃ bḥavatīti nāvaśyaṃ vākyadvayaprayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: 3. Likewise, even through disagreement, the understanding of positive concomitance follows. For without it, the absence of the reason in the absence of the probandum would not be established. 'Likewise' means: just as in the statement of positive concomitance, so too by implication alone, in formulation through disagreement, the understanding of positive concomitance, though not explicitly stated, follows. For without that positive concomitance being grasped by the intellect, there would be no ascertainment of the absence of the reason in the absence of the probandum. Therefore, even by a single statement, whether formulated through positive concomitance or negative concomitance, the presence and absence of the logical mark in the similar and dissimilar cases is declared. Hence it is not necessary to employ two statements.

body.text: 4. tatrānupalabdheḥ sādharmyavān prayogaḥ yad yatropalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ san nopalabhyate sa tatrāsadvyavahāraviṣayaḥ / yathā śaśaśirasi śṛṅgaṃ / nopalabhyate ca kvacitpradeśaviśeṣa upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpto ghaṭa iti / atra dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇaḥ śaśaśirasaḥ sādhyadharmiṇaś ca pradeśaviśeṣasyopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptapratiṣedhyānupalambhahetukṛtaṃ sādṛśyam abhidheyam //
body.translated_text: 4. Therein, the formulation by agreement of non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) is: 'Whatever, being such that it fulfills the conditions of apprehension, is not apprehended in a given place, is the object of the convention of non-existence there. For example, horns on a hare's head. And a pot fulfilling the conditions of apprehension is not apprehended in a certain particular location.' Here, the similarity produced by the logical reason—the non-apprehension of what is to be negated that fulfills the conditions of apprehension—between the example (hare's head) and the subject (particular location) is what is to be stated.

body.text: 5. tathā svabhāvahetoḥ prayogaḥ / yat sat tat sarvam anityaṃ yathā ghaṭaḥ saṃś ca śabdaḥ / śuddhasya svabhāvasya prayogaḥ / sattvamātrasyopadhyanapekṣatvāt / yad utpattimat tad anityam / yathā ghaṭaḥ / utpattimac ca sukham ity avyatiriktaviśeṣaṇasya / utpattir hi svarūpalābhaḥ / sā ca bhāvasyātmabhūtaiva kevalaṃ kalpanayā vyatirekiṇīva pradarśyate / yat kṛtakaṃ tad anityaṃ yathā ghaṭaḥ kṛtakaś ca śabda iti vyatiriktaviśeṣaṇasya / apekṣitaparavyāpāro hi svabhāvaniṣpattau bhāvaḥ kṛtaka iti / evaṃ pratyayabhedabheditvādayo draṣṭavyāḥ / atra hi dṛṣṭāntadharmibhiḥ sādhyadharmiṇāṃ hetukṛtaṃ sādṛśyam abhidheyam / sarva ete sādhanadharmā yathāsvaṃ
body.translated_text: 5. Likewise, the formulation of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (essential nature reason): 'Whatever exists is entirely impermanent, like a pot; and sound exists.' This is the formulation of the pure essential nature, since mere existence does not depend on any additional condition. 'Whatever is produced is impermanent, like a pot; and pleasure is produced'—this is for a non-different qualifier, for production is the acquisition of one's own nature, and that is indeed the very essence of an entity; it is only through conceptual construction that it appears as if different. 'Whatever is made is impermanent, like a pot; and sound is made'—this is for a different qualifier, for an entity that requires the activity of another for the accomplishment of its own nature is called 'made.' Similarly, 'being divisible by difference of conditions' and so forth should be understood. Here, the similarity produced by the logical reason between the examples and the subject is what is to be stated. All these proving properties, each in its own way

body.text: pramāṇaiḥ siddhasādhanadharmamātrānubandha eva sādhyadharme 'vagantavyāḥ / vastutas tasyaiva tatsvabhāvatvāt / tanniṣpattāv aniṣpannasya tatsvabhāvatvāyogāt / viruddhadharmādhyāsasya bhedaIakṣaṇatvāt //
body.translated_text: is to be understood as [the reason] being connected only with the property established by the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) that is the property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharma</s>). In reality, because that [property to be proved] has that very nature. Because what has not come into being when that [thing] comes into being cannot have the nature of that [thing]. Because the superimposition of contradictory properties is the defining characteristic of difference.

body.text: 6. kāryahetoḥ sādharmyavān prayogaḥ / yatra yatra dhūmas tatra tatra vahnir yathā mahānase / dhūmas cātra / atra dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇo mahānasasya sādhyadharmiṇaś ca pradeśaviśeṣasya dhūmahetukṛtaṃ sādṛśyam abhidheyam / ihāpi tribhir anupalambhair dvābhyāṃ pratyakṣābhyāṃ siddhe kāryakāraṇabhave kāraṇe sādhye kāryahetur vaktavyaḥ / anupalabdher vaidharmyavān prayogaḥ / yat sad upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃtad upalabhyata eva / yathā nīlaviśeṣaḥ / na caivam ihopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya ghaṭasyopalabdhir iti / atra hi dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇo nilaviśeṣasya sādhyadharmiṇaś ca pradeśasyopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaniṣedhyānupalambhākhyahetukṛtaṃ vaisādṛśyam abhidheyam /
body.translated_text: 6. The formulation with positive concomitance (<s>sādharmya</s>) of the effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>): "Wherever there is smoke, there is fire, as in the kitchen. And there is smoke here." Here, the similarity produced by the reason of smoke between the example-subject (the kitchen) and the subject to be proved (the particular location) is what is to be stated. Here too, when the cause-effect relationship is established through three non-apprehensions and two direct perceptions, and the cause is to be proved, the effect-reason should be stated. The formulation with negative concomitance (<s>vaidharmya</s>) of non-apprehension: "Whatever exists and fulfills the conditions of apprehension is indeed apprehended, like a particular [shade of] blue. But here there is no apprehension of the pot which fulfills the conditions of apprehension." Here, the dissimilarity produced by the reason called non-apprehension-of-that-which-fulfills-the-conditions-of-apprehension between the example-subject (the particular blue) and the subject to be proved (the location) is what is to be stated.

body.text: 7. svabhāvahetor vaidharmyavantaḥ prayogāḥ asaty anityatve nāsti kvacit sattvaṃ yathā gaganamaline / saṃś ca śabdaḥ / asaty anityatve na kvacid utpattimattvaṃ yathākāśe / utpattimac ca sukham / asaty anityatve na kvacit kṛtakatvaṃ yathā kurmaromni / kṛtakaś ca śabda iti / atra dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇā sādhyadharmiṇo hetukṛtaṃ vaisadṛśyam abhidheyam //
body.translated_text: 7. Formulations with negative concomitance of the nature-reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>): "In the absence of impermanence, there is nowhere existence, as with a sky-flower. And sound exists." "In the absence of impermanence, there is nowhere the state of having originated, as with space. And pleasure has originated." "In the absence of impermanence, there is nowhere the state of being produced, as with a tortoise-hair. And sound is produced." Here, the dissimilarity between the example-subject and the subject to be proved, produced by the reason, is what is to be stated.

body.text: 8. kāryahetor vaidharmyavān prayogaḥ / asaty agnau na bhavaty eva dhūmo yathā mahāhrade / dhūmaś cātreti /
body.translated_text: 8. The formulation with negative concomitance of the effect-reason: "In the absence of fire, there is certainly no smoke, as in a great lake. And there is smoke here."

body.text: atra dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇā sādhyadharmiṇo hetukṛtaṃ vaisadṛśyam abhidheyam //
body.translated_text: Here, the dissimilarity between the example-subject and the subject to be proved, produced by the reason, is what is to be stated.

body.text: 9. trirūpaliṅgākhyānaṃ parārtham anumānam ity arthān na pakṣādivacanam anumānam uktaṃ bhavati / tatra pratijñā tāvan na sākṣāt sādhanam / arthād evārthagateḥ / artha eva hy arthaṃ gamayati pratibandhān / nābhidhānaṃ viparyayāt / pāraṃparyeṇāpi na bhavati / sādhyasyaivābhidhānāt / sādhyasādhanadharmaviśeṣopadarśanārtham anavayavabhūtāpi pratijñā dṛṣṭāntavat prayujyata iti cet / na / evaṃ hy anujñādivākyam api prayoktavyaṃ syāt / na hi tair vinā eva sādhanasya pravṛttir saṃbhavati / viṣayopadarśanam api niṣphalam / tenāpi vinā sādhyapratīteḥ / tathā hi yat kṛtakaṃ tat sarvam anityaṃ kṛtakaś ca śabda ity etāvanmātre prayukte 'nityaḥ śabda iti pratītir bhavaty evāntareṇa pratijñāvacanam / nanv asati pratijñāvacane sapakṣādivyavasthā katham / tathā hi sādhyadharmasāmānyena samāno 'rthaḥ sapakṣaḥ / tadabhāvaprabhāvitaś cāsapakṣa iti / asati hi pratijñānirdeśe pakṣāpekṣānibandhanaṃ trairūpyaṃ nāstīti / asad etat / tathā hi pratijñāvacanam antareṇāpi sarvaṃ saṃpadyata eva / upanaya

body.translated_text: 9. The statement of the triple-characterized mark (<s>trirūpaliṅga</s>) is inference for others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>) — in this sense, the [mere] statement of the thesis and the like is not called inference. In this regard, the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>) is not directly a means of proof, because the meaning is understood from the meaning itself. For it is the [real] object that leads to [the knowledge of another] object, through invariable connection — not the verbal expression, because of the possibility of error. Nor [is the thesis a means of proof] even indirectly, because it merely states what is to be proved. [Objection:] The thesis, though not a member [of the syllogism], is employed like the example for the purpose of showing the specific properties of what is to be proved and the means of proof. No. For then even a statement of permission and the like would have to be employed. For without those, the operation of the proof is indeed possible. The indication of the subject matter is also futile, because the thing to be proved is understood even without it. For when only this much is stated — "Whatever is produced is impermanent, and sound is produced" — the understanding that "sound is impermanent" arises even without the statement of the thesis. [Objection:] Without the statement of the thesis, how is the determination of the similar instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>) and the like [to be made]? For the similar instance is an object that shares the general property to be proved, and the dissimilar instance is determined by the absence of that [property]. Without the indication of the thesis, the triple characterization, which depends on the thesis, does not exist. This is incorrect. For even without the statement of the thesis, everything is accomplished. The application (<s>upanaya</s>)

When even one of the three characteristics is unstated, [there is] a pseudo-reason (<s>sādhanābhāsa</s>). Even when stated, if it is unestablished or doubtful, for [both] the proponent

body.text: 11. tatraikasya rūpasya dharmisaṃbandhasyāsiddhau saṃdehe cāsiddho hetvābhāsaḥ / yathā śabdasyānityatve sādhye cākṣuṣatvam ubhayāsiddham / cetanās tarava iti sādhye sarvatvagapaharaṇe maraṇaṃ prativādyasiddham / vijñānendriyāyurnirodhaIakṣaṇasya maraṇasyānenābhyupagamāt / acetanāḥ sukhādaya iti sādhya utpattimattvam anityatvaṃ vā sāṃkhyasya svayaṃvādino 'siddham / atra cotpattimattvam anityatvaṃ vā paryāyeṇa hetur na yugapat tathā hi parārtho hetūpanyāsaḥ / parasya cāsata utpāda utpattimattvaṃ sataś ca niranvayo vināśo 'nityatvaṃ siddham iti / tathā svayaṃ tadāśrayaṇasya vā saṃdehe 'siddhaḥ / yathā bāspādibhāvena saṃdigdho bhūtasaṃghāto 'gnisiddhau bhūtānāṃ pṛthivyādīnāṃ saṃghātaḥ samūho 'gnisiddhyartham upādīyamāno 'siddhaḥ / yathā ceha nikūñjemayūraḥ kekāyitād iti tadāpātadeśavibhrame / āpātanam āpātas tasya kekāyitasyāpāta utpādas tasya deśas tasya vibhramo bhrāntiḥ / atha vā āpataty āgacchaty asmād ity āpātaḥ / sa eva deśas tadāpātadeśaḥ / tasya vibhrame / yat punar ucyate 'nyair āpāta āgamanam iti tad ayuktam /
body.translated_text: 11. Therein, when one characteristic — the connection with the subject (<s>dharmisaṃbandha</s>) — is unestablished or doubtful, [there is] an unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>) pseudo-reason. For example, when the impermanence of sound is to be proved, visibility is unestablished for both [parties]. When the thesis is "trees are sentient," the [reason] "death upon complete removal of bark" is unestablished for the opponent, because he does not accept that death — which is characterized by the cessation of consciousness, sense-faculties, and vital force — [applies to trees]. When the thesis is "pleasure and the like are non-sentient," the [reason] "having originated" or "impermanence" is unestablished for the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> proponent. Here, "having originated" or "impermanence" is the reason alternately, not simultaneously, because the presentation of the reason is for others, and for others, origination as the arising of what did not exist and impermanence as the traceless destruction of what exists are [already] established. Likewise, [the reason is] unestablished when there is doubt about itself or its substratum. For example, a collection of elements (<s>bhūtasaṃghāta</s>), doubtful as to whether it is steam or the like, is unestablished when employed for the purpose of proving fire — "the collection of elements, namely earth and the like, [constituting the assemblage]" is unestablished [as a basis for proving fire]. And as [in the example]: "In this thicket there is a peacock, because of [its] cry" — when there is an error regarding the location of origin [of the sound]. "Origin" (<s>āpāta</s>) means the place of origin of that cry; the error regarding that place is the confusion. Or "<s>āpāta</s>" means "that from which [the sound] comes." That very [place] is the location; the error regarding that location. Now, what others say — that "<s>āpāta</s>" means "arrival" — that is incorrect.

body.text: na hi śrotrendriyasya prāpyakāritā ghaṭate / nāpīdaṃ bauddhadarśanam / tathā hy uktam abhidharmakośe /
body.translated_text: For the contact-requiring operation of the auditory sense-organ is not tenable. Nor is this the Buddhist doctrine. For it is stated in the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>:

body.text: cakṣuḥśrotramano 'prāptaviṣayaṃ trayam anyatheti /
body.translated_text: "The eye, ear, and mind — three [sense-faculties] — apprehend objects without contact; the others [do so] otherwise."

body.text: āśrayāsiddhyāpy asiddhaḥ / yathā sarvagata ātmā sarvatropalabhyamānaguṇatvād ākāśavat / sarvatropalabhyamānaguṇāḥ sukhādayo yasya tadbhāvas tattvaṃ / tasmād yady ayam ātmā sarvagato na bhavet / kathaṃ dakṣiṇāpatha upalabdhāḥ sukhādayo madhyadeśa upalabhyante / ākāśavad iti dṛṣṭānte ākāśasya guṇaḥ śabdaḥ / sa ca yathā vikāriṇi puruṣa upalabhyate tathānyatrāpīti / syād eṣa hetur yadi bauddhasya sarvatropalabhyamānaguṇatvam ātmanaḥ siddhaṃ syāt / yāvad ātmaiva na siddhaḥ // tad evam asiddhaḥ ṣaṭprakāraḥ // // //
body.translated_text: Also unestablished due to the unestablishment of the substratum: for example, "The self is omnipresent, because of having qualities apprehended everywhere, like space." "Having qualities apprehended everywhere" — qualities such as pleasure and the like [are said to belong to one] whose nature is such. Therefore, if this self were not omnipresent, how could pleasures and the like experienced in the Southern region be experienced in the Central region? "Like space" — the quality of space is sound, and just as it is experienced in the changing person, so too elsewhere. This reason would hold if, for the Buddhist, the omnipresence of the self's qualities were established. But the self itself is not even established [for the Buddhist]. Thus the unestablished [pseudo-reason] is of six kinds.

body.text: 12. tathaikasya rūpasyāsapakṣe 'sattvasyāsiddhāv anaikāntiko hetvābhāsaḥ / yathā śabdasya nityatvādike dharme sādhye prameya
body.translated_text: 12. Likewise, when one characteristic — the non-existence [of the reason] in the dissimilar instance (<s>asapakṣa</s>) — is unestablished, [there is] an inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) pseudo-reason. For example, when permanence or the like of sound is to be proved, the property of being a <s>prameya</s>

body.text: diko dharmaḥ sapakṣavipakṣayoḥ sarvatraikadeśe ca vartamānaḥ / nityatvādika ity ātrādiśabdena prayatnānantarīyakatvāprayatnānantarīyakatvayor grahaṇam / prameyatvādika ity atrādiśabdenānityatvāsparśatvayor grahaṇam / kiṃbhūtaḥ prameyatvādiko dharmo 'naikāntikaḥ / sapakṣavipakṣayoḥ sarvatraikadeśe ca vartamānaḥ / nityaḥ śabdaḥ prameyatvād ity atra nityatve sādhye prameyatvaṃ sapakṣavipakṣayor vartate / ekadeśe ca vartamāna ity atrāpi sapakṣavipakṣayor iti saṃbandhanīyaṃ / caśabdenaitat kathayati / na kevalaṃ sapakṣavipakṣavyāpi
body.translated_text: and the like, existing in both similar and dissimilar instances, and also in part [of each]. "Permanence and the like" — here the word "and the like" (<s>ādi</s>) includes [the properties of] being caused by effort and not being caused by effort. "Being a knowable object and the like" — here the word "and the like" includes impermanence and intangibility. What kind of property is "being a knowable object and the like" that makes it an inconclusive [pseudo-reason]? It exists in both similar and dissimilar instances, and also in part [of each]. "Sound is permanent because it is a knowable object" — here, when permanence is to be proved, the property of being knowable exists in both similar and dissimilar instances. "And existing in part" — here too, "in similar and dissimilar instances" should be connected. By the word "and" this is stated: not only is the pervasion of knowability in both similar and dissimilar instances an inconclusive pseudo-reason,

body.text: prameyatvam anaikāntiko hetvābhāsaḥ / yo 'pi sapakṣavyāpī vipakṣaikadeśavṛttiḥ / tathā vipakṣavyāpī sapakṣaikadeśavṛttīḥ / yo vā sapakṣavipakṣayor ekadeśavṛttiḥ sarvo 'sāv anaikāntiko hetvābhāsa iti / tatra prayatnānantariyakaḥ śabdo 'nityatvād ghaṭavad ity ayaṃ vipakṣaikadeśavṛttiḥ / vidyuti vartamān
body.translated_text: but also [a reason] that pervades the similar instance and exists in part of the dissimilar instance, likewise one that pervades the dissimilar instance and exists in part of the similar instance, and one that exists in part of both similar and dissimilar instances — all of these are inconclusive pseudo-reasons. Among these, "sound is caused by effort, because of impermanence, like a pot" — this [reason] exists in part of the dissimilar instance [only], being present in lightning
