body.text: āt sapakṣavyāpī tu bhavaty eva / sarvasya prayatnānantarīyakasyānityatvāt / aprayatnānantarīyakaḥ śabdo 'nityatvād vidyud iva / ayaṃ sapakṣaikadeśavṛttiḥ / aprayatnānantarīyako 'sya sapakṣo 'vidyudākāśādiḥ / tatrānityatvaṃ vidyuti vartate nākāśādau / vipakṣavyāpītu bhavaty eva / sarvaprayatnānantarīyake 'nityatvasya gatatvāt / nityaḥ śabdo 'sparśatvāt paraśuvat / asparśatvaṃ hi vipakṣaikadeśe buddhyādau sapakṣaikadeśe cākāśādau vartata ity ubhayapakṣaikadeśavṛttiḥ / evaṃ caturvidhaḥ sādhāraṇānaikāntiko nirdiṣṭaḥ //
body.translated_text: Yet it does pervade the <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar instance) — since everything produced by effort is impermanent. [Example:] 'Sound is impermanent because it is not produced by effort, like lightning.' This is present in only part of the <s>sapakṣa</s>. The <s>sapakṣa</s> of what is not produced by effort includes non-lightning, space, and the like. Among those, impermanence is present in lightning but not in space and the like. And it does pervade the <s>vipakṣa</s> (dissimilar instance) — since impermanence has been established in everything produced by effort. [Example:] 'Sound is permanent because it is intangible, like an axe.' For intangibility is present in part of the <s>vipakṣa</s> — in intellect and the like — and in part of the <s>sapakṣa</s> — in space and the like. Thus it is present in only part of both sides. Thus, the fourfold <s>sādhāraṇānaikāntika</s> (common inconclusive reason) has been described.

body.text: 13. tathā 'syaiva rūpasya saṃdehe 'py anaikāntika eva / yathā sarvajñaḥ kaścid vivakṣitaḥ puruṣo rāgādimān veti sādhye vaktṛtvādiko dharmaḥ saṃdigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttikaḥ / sarvatraikadeśe vā sarvajño vaktā nopalabhyata iti / evaṃ prakārasyānupalambhasyādṛṣyātmaviṣayatvena saṃdehahetutvāt / asarvajñaviparyayād vaktṛtvāder vyāvṛttiḥ saṃdigdhā //
body.translated_text: 13. Likewise, even when there is doubt about the same form [i.e., the logical characteristic], it is indeed inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). For example, when the <s>sādhya</s> (property to be proven) is 'a certain person under consideration is omniscient or possesses desire and so forth,' a property like 'being a speaker' has doubtful exclusion from the <s>vipakṣa</s>. For a speaker who is omniscient is not found either universally or in any particular instance. Since a non-apprehension of this kind, having an imperceptible subject, is a cause of doubt, the exclusion of being a speaker and the like from the opposite of the omniscient is doubtful.

body.text: 14. dvayo rūpayor viparyayasiddhau viruddhaḥ / kayor dvayoḥ / sapakṣe sattvasyāsapakṣe cāsattvasya yathā kṛtakatvaṃ prayatnānantarīyakatvaṃ ca nityatve sādhye viruddhahetvābhāsaḥ // dvayor upādānam asapakṣavyāpyasapakṣaikadeśavṛttitvena bhedāt / anayoḥ
body.translated_text: 14. When the reverse of both characteristics is established, [the reason] is contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>). Which two? The presence in the <s>sapakṣa</s> and the absence in the <s>asapakṣa</s> (dissimilar instance). For example, 'being produced' (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) and 'being produced by effort' (<s>prayatnānantarīyakatva</s>), when the <s>sādhya</s> is permanence — these are fallacious reasons of the contradictory type. 'Two' is mentioned because there is a distinction between what pervades the <s>asapakṣa</s> and what is present in only part of the <s>asapakṣa</s>.

body.text: sapakṣe 'sattvam asapakṣe ca sattvam iti viparyayasiddhiḥ / etau sādhyaviparyayasādhanād viruddhau // dvayo rūpayor ekasyāsiddhāv aparasya ca saṃdehe 'naikāntikaḥ / dvayor ity anvayavyatirekayoḥ / ekasyāsiddhāv iti / asapakṣe 'sattvasya / aparasya saṃdeha iti sapakṣe sattvasya / yathā vītarāgaḥ sarvajño vā vaktṛtvād iti / vyatireko 'trāsiddhaḥ saṃdigdho 'nvayaḥ / sarvajñavītarāgayor viprakarṣād vacanādes tatra sattvam asattvaṃ vā saṃdigdham / anayor eva dvayo rūpayoḥ saṃdehe 'naikāntikaḥ / yathā sātmakaṃ jīvaccharīraṃ prāṇādimattvād iti / na hi sātmakānatmakābhyām anyo rāśir asti yatra praṇādir va
body.translated_text: For these, the reverse is established: presence in the <s>sapakṣa</s> [becomes] absence, and absence in the <s>asapakṣa</s> [becomes] presence. These two are contradictory because they prove the opposite of the <s>sādhya</s>. When, of the two characteristics, one is unestablished and the other is doubtful, [the reason] is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). 'Of the two' means of the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) and the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>). 'One being unestablished' means the absence in the <s>asapakṣa</s>. 'The other being doubtful' means the presence in the <s>sapakṣa</s>. For example: 'Someone is free from desire, or omniscient, because of being a speaker.' Here the <s>vyatireka</s> is unestablished and the <s>anvaya</s> is doubtful. Since those free from desire and the omniscient are far apart, the presence or absence of speech and the like therein is doubtful. When both of these very same two characteristics are doubtful, [the reason] is inconclusive. For example: 'A living body has a self, because it possesses breath and the like.' For there is no other category apart from what has a self and what lacks a self in which breath and the like

body.text: r
body.translated_text: would

body.text: tate / nāpy anayor ekatra vṛttiniścayaḥ / ata evānvayavyatirekayoḥ saṃdehād anaikāntikaḥ / sādhyetarayor ato niścayābhavāt /
body.translated_text: exist. Nor is there certainty of its existence in either one. For this very reason, due to doubt about both the <s>anvaya</s> and the <s>vyatireka</s>, it is inconclusive — because of the absence of certainty about either the <s>sādhya</s> or its opposite.

body.text: 15. evam eteṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ rūpāṇāṃ ekaikasya dvayor dvayor vā rūpayor asiddhau saṃdehe ca yathāyogam asiddhaviruddhānaikāntikās trayo hetvābhāsāḥ / evam anantaroktena krameṇa trayo hetvābhasaḥ / asiddhaviruddhānaikāntikāḥ / trāyāṇāṃ rūpāṇāṃ pakṣadharmānvayavyatirekākhyānāṃ madhye / ekaikasya rūpasyāsiddhau saṃdehe ca / tathā dvayor dvayor vā rūpayor asiddhau saṃdehe ca yathāyogam iti yathāsaṃbhavam / tatra dharmisaṃbandhasyaikasya rūpasyāsiddhāv asiddhaḥ / tathā sapakṣe sattvasyāsiddhau saṃdehe cānaikāntika uktaḥ / evam ekaikasya rūpasyāsiddhau saṃdehe cāsiddho 'naikāntikaś ca hetvābhāsa
body.translated_text: 15. Thus, for each one of these three characteristics, or for any two of them, when there is non-establishment or doubt, the three fallacious reasons — unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), and inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) — [arise] as appropriate. Thus, by the order just stated, the three fallacious reasons are: unestablished, contradictory, and inconclusive. Among the three characteristics named property-of-the-subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>), positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>), and negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) — when any one of these is unestablished or doubtful, and likewise when any two are unestablished or doubtful, as appropriate and as possible: when the single characteristic of the connection with the subject (<s>dharmisaṃbandha</s>) is unestablished, [the reason] is unestablished. Similarly, when the presence in the <s>sapakṣa</s> is unestablished or doubtful, [the reason] is stated as inconclusive. Thus, when each single characteristic is unestablished or doubtful, unestablished and inconclusive fallacious reasons

body.text: uktaḥ / tathā dvayor dvayo rūpayor viparyayasiddhau viruddho hetvābhāsa uktaḥ / asapakṣe sattvasya ca saṃdehe vā 'naikāntika uktaḥ / tathā sapakṣāsapakṣayor api hetoḥ sadasattvasaṃdehe 'naikāntika eva / evaṃ dvayor dvayor asiddhau saṃdehe ca viruddho 'naikāntikaś ca hetvābhāsa iti /
body.translated_text: have been stated. Likewise, when the reverse of both characteristics is established, the contradictory fallacious reason has been stated. When there is doubt about the presence in the <s>asapakṣa</s>, it is stated as inconclusive. Similarly, when the reason's presence and absence in both the <s>sapakṣa</s> and <s>asapakṣa</s> are doubtful, it is indeed inconclusive. Thus, when two characteristics are unestablished or doubtful, the contradictory and inconclusive fallacious reasons [are obtained].

body.text: 16. nanu katham uktaṃ trayo hetvābhāsā iti / yāvatā vaiphalyam api hetoḥ pṛthagdūṣaṇam asti / tad uktam /
body.translated_text: 16. But how was it said that there are [only] three fallacious reasons? For futility (<s>vaiphalya</s>) is also a separate fault of the reason. As it is stated:

children.text: sādhanaṃ yad vivādena nyastaṃ tac cen na sādhyate /
children.translated_text: 'If a proof proposed in a dispute does not prove [what is to be proven],

children.text: kiṃ sādhyam anyathāniṣṭaṃ bhaved vaiphalyam eva vā // iti
children.translated_text: would it prove something undesired otherwise, or would it simply be futile?'

body.text: atra kecid āhuḥ satyam asty eva vaiphalyaṃ hetoḥ pṛthagdūṣaṇaṃ / yat punar asiddhaviruddhānaikāntikakathanaṃ viniścayādau tad asāmarthyaprabhedena / dvividhaṃ hi sādhanasya dūṣaṇaṃ bhavati / asāmarthyaṃ vaiyarthyaṃ ca / asāmarthyaṃ tv asiddhaviruddhānaikantikabhedāt trividham / vaiyarthyaṃ tv ekam eveti / syād etad yadi vaiyarthyaṃ nāma heto

children.translated_text: One might say: 'If pointlessness were a fault of the reason —'

children.text: dūṣaṇaṃ syāt kiṃ tu pramāṇasya / tad uktam udyotakareṇāpi / adhigatam api gamayatā pramāṇena piṣṭaṃ piṣṭaṃ syād iti / nyāyaparameśvarair api kīrttipādair uktam /
children.translated_text: but rather it is [a fault] of the <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition). As stated by <s>Udyotakara</s>: 'When a <s>pramāṇa</s> causes one to know what is already known, it would be grinding what is already ground.' And as stated by the supreme master of logic, <s>Kīrtipāda</s> (<s>Dharmakīrti</s>):

body.translated_text: Here some say: 'Truly, futility is indeed a separate fault of the reason. But the enumeration of unestablished, contradictory, and inconclusive is given [in the <s>Viniścaya</s> and other works] as a classification of incapacity. For the fault of a proof is twofold: incapacity (<s>asāmarthya</s>) and pointlessness (<s>vaiyarthya</s>). Incapacity is threefold, through the divisions of unestablished, contradictory, and inconclusive. But pointlessness is just one.'

body.text:
niṣpāditakriye kaścid viśeṣam asamādadhat /
karmaṇy aindriyam anyad vā sādhanaṃ kim itīṣyata iti
body.translated_text: 'When the function has already been accomplished, [a cognition] that adds no special [knowledge] — whether it be a sensory cognition or another proof — why is it desired as an instrument?'

body.text: tataś ca katham idaṃ vaiyarthyaṃ hetor dūṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: Therefore, how is this pointlessness a fault of the reason?

body.text: athaivam ucyate pramāṇājanakatvād dhetur api vyartha ucyata iti / evaṃ hi vāstavam idaṃ hetor na dūṣaṇaṃ syāt / vāstavaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ vaktavyaṃ / kiṃ ca / yadi vaiyarthyaṃ hetor dūṣanaṃ bhinnaṃ syāt / yathāsiddhatāpratipakṣeṇa heto rūpaṃ pakṣadharmatā / viruddhatāpratipakṣeṇānvayaḥ / anaikāntikatāpratipakṣena ca vyatirekaś coktaḥ / tathā vaiyarthyapratipakṣeṇāpy anyad rūpam uktaṃ syāt / na cānyad rūpaṃ hetor ghaṭate / yadi tarhīdaṃ vaiyarthyaṃ na pṛthagdūṣaṇaṃ kathaṃ tarhy anena vādī nigṛhyate //
body.translated_text: If it is said that because it does not produce a <s>pramāṇa</s>, the reason too is called futile — then this would not be a real fault of the reason. A real fault should be stated. Moreover, if pointlessness were a separate fault of the reason, then just as the form of the reason called 'property-of-the-subject' is the counterpart of unestablishedness, 'positive concomitance' is the counterpart of contradictoriness, and 'negative concomitance' is the counterpart of inconclusiveness, so too there would need to be another form [of the reason] as the counterpart of pointlessness. But no other form of the reason is possible. If then this pointlessness is not a separate fault, how is the disputant defeated by it?

body.text: 17. atra kecid āhuḥ / asiddha eva vaiyarthyaṃ
body.translated_text: 17. Here some say: 'Pointlessness is subsumed

body.text: antar
body.translated_text: within

body.text: bhavatīti / tathā hi jijñāsitaviśeṣo dharmī pakṣaḥ / taddharmaś ca hetuḥ / tato 'pakṣadharmatvād vaiyarthyam asiddha evāntaryāti / anye tu sudhiya evam āhuḥ / nedaṃ hetor dūṣaṇaṃ kiṃ tu parārthānumāne vaktur api guṇadoṣā
body.translated_text: the unestablished itself.' For the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>) about which a specific property is being investigated is the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>). And its property is the reason. Therefore, since it is not a property of the thesis, pointlessness falls within the unestablished. But other intelligent ones say thus: 'This is not a fault of the reason, but in inference-for-others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>), the merits and faults of the speaker are also considered.'

body.text: ś cintyante
body.translated_text: Thus

body.text: iti viphalābhidhāyī apratibhayaiva nigṛhyata iti / tathā hi prakṛtam eva sādhyaṃ nāprakṛtam iti sādhyatāyāḥ prakṛter niyāmaka eṣa panthā / evaṃ kṛtvā parisaṃkhyānaṃ na virudhyate / doṣāḥ punar nyūnatvam asiddhir vādinā sādhayitum iṣṭasyārthasya viparyayasādhanam aṣṭādaśa dṛṣṭāntadoṣāś ceti / atra ca yac codyaṃ parihāraśca tad granthavistarabhayān na likhitam iti / sthitam etad
body.translated_text: the speaker of a futile statement is defeated simply by his lack of eloquence. For the principle that 'only what is under consideration is the <s>sādhya</s>, not what is not under consideration' is the rule that determines the proper nature of what is to be proven. With this understanding, the enumeration is not violated. The faults are: deficiency (<s>nyūnatva</s>), non-establishment of what the disputant wishes to prove, proving the opposite of the intended object, and the eighteen faults of examples (<s>dṛṣṭāntadoṣa</s>). The objections and responses regarding this are not written here, due to fear of the length of the work. It is settled

body.text: yadi vaiyarthyaṃ hetor dūṣaṇaṃ tadāsiddha evāntarbhavati / no ced apratibhayaiveti //
body.translated_text: that if pointlessness is a fault of the reason, then it falls within the unestablished itself; and if it is not, [the speaker is defeated] simply by lack of eloquence.

body.text: 18. triIakṣaṇo hetur uktas tāvatārthapratītir iti na pṛthag dṛṣṭānto nāma sādhanāvayavaḥ kaścit / tena nāsya lakṣaṇaṃ pṛthag ucyate gatārthatvāt / hetoḥ sapakṣa eva sattvam asapakṣāc ca sarvato vyāvṛttī rūpam uktam abhedena i punar aviśeṣeṇa kāryasvabhāvayor janmatanmātrānubandhau darśanīyāv uktau / rūpaśabdaḥ pratyekam abhisaṃbadhyate / hetoḥ sapakṣa eva sattvam iti sādhyenānugatam idam ekaṃ rūpam asapakṣāc ca sarvato vyāvṛttir iti sādhyanivṛttyā nivṛttir asya dvitīyaṃ rūpam uktam / abhedeneti svabhāvādihetum akṛtvā / janmatanmātre saty anubaddhau / sādhānaṃ kṛteti samāsaḥ / tac ca darśayatā dhūmas tatrāgnir iti asaty agnau na kvacid dhumo yathā mahānasetarayoḥ / yatra kṛtakatvaṃ tatrānityatvam anityatvābhāve kṛtakatvāsaṃbhavo yathā ghaṭākāśayor iti darśanīyam / na hy anyathā sapakṣavipakṣayoḥ sadasattve yathoktaprakāre śakye darśayituṃ / tatkāryatāniyamaḥ kāryaliṅgasya ca svabhāvavyāptiḥ / tasyāgnyādeḥ kāryaṃ tatkāryaṃ tasya bhāvas tatkāryatā / na hy anyathā śakyo darśayitum iti liṅgavacanavipariṇāmena sambandhanīyam //
body.translated_text: 18. The reason has been stated as having three characteristics (<s>trilakṣaṇa</s>). 'To that extent, there is cognition of the object' — thus example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) is not a separate member of the proof. Therefore, its definition is not stated separately, as it would be redundant. The form of the reason — its presence only in the <s>sapakṣa</s> and its complete exclusion from the <s>asapakṣa</s> — has been stated without distinction. But specifically, for the two types of reasons — causal (<s>kārya</s>) and essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) — the connection through birth and mere-being-that must be demonstrated. The word 'form' (<s>rūpa</s>) is connected with each individually. 'The presence of the reason only in the <s>sapakṣa</s>' — this, as accompanied by the <s>sādhya</s>, is one form. 'And its complete exclusion from the <s>asapakṣa</s>' — this exclusion by the cessation of the <s>sādhya</s> is the second form stated. 'Without distinction' means without differentiating between reasons of essential nature and the like. When there is birth and mere-being-that, [the reason] is connected. [The word] 'proof (<s>sādhana</s>) has been done' — thus the compound. And one demonstrating this [shows]: 'Where there is smoke, there is fire; where there is no fire, there is no smoke anywhere — as in a great lake versus other [places]. Where there is produced-ness, there is impermanence; where there is an absence of impermanence, produced-ness is impossible — as in a pot versus space.' This must be demonstrated. For otherwise, the presence and absence in <s>sapakṣa</s> and <s>vipakṣa</s> of the stated kind cannot be shown. The determination of the being-an-effect-thereof and the essential-nature-pervasion of the causal mark: that which is its effect is 'its-effect' (<s>tatkārya</s>); its nature is 'being-its-effect' (<s>tatkāryatā</s>). For it cannot otherwise be shown — this should be connected by the transposition of the mark-statement.

body.text: 19. asmiṃś cārthe darśite darśita eva dṛṣṭānto bhavati / etāvanmātratvāt tasyeti / etenaiva dṛṣṭāntadoṣā api nirastā bhavanti / etenaiveti hetulakṣaṇābhidhānenaiva dṛṣṭāntasyāpi sāmarthyād gatārthatvena dṛṣṭāntadoṣā
body.translated_text: 19. When this meaning is demonstrated, the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) is also demonstrated — since the example consists of just that much. By this very [principle], the defects of the example are also refuted. By 'this very' — meaning by the very statement of the definition of the logical reason (<s>hetu</s>), since the meaning of the example too is implicitly understood through its capacity,

body.text: api sādhanatvena pratyākhyātā bhavanti / yena hetoḥ sāmānyaviśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ yathoktaṃ pradarśyate
body.translated_text: the defects of the example are also rejected as means of proof. The general and specific characteristics of the reason by which are demonstrated as stated —

body.text: sa
body.translated_text: that

body.text: saṃyagdṛṣṭāntaḥ / yena punas tasya lakṣaṇadvayaṃ na pradarśyate so dṛṣṭāntābhāsa ity uktaṃ bhavati / yathā nityaḥ śabdaḥ / amūrtatvāt / karmavad iti sādhyadharmavikalo dṛṣṭāntābhāsaḥ / atra hi karmaṇi nityatvaṃ sādhyadharmo nāsti / anityatvāt karmanaḥ / amūrtatvaṃ hi sādhanadharmo 'sti / amūrtatvād asya / nityaḥ śabdaḥ / amūrtatvāt paramāṇuvad iti / sādhanadharmavikalaḥ / sādhyadharmo 'tra nityatvam asti nityatvāt paramāṇoḥ / nityaḥ śabdo 'mūrtatvād ghaṭavad iti / ubhayadharmavikalo 'nityatvān mūrtatvād ghaṭasya / rāgādimān ayaṃ puruṣo vacanāt / rathyāpuruṣavat / saṃdigdhasādhyadharmo 'yaṃ dṛṣṭāntābhāsaḥ / rathyāpuruṣe vacanaṃ pratyakṣeṇaiva niścitam iti sādhanadharmas tatra siddhaḥ / sādhyadharmas tu rāgādimatvaṃ saṃdigdham / maraṇadharmā 'yaṃ puruṣaḥ / rāgādimatvād rathyāpuruṣavat / rathyāpuruṣe maraṇadharmatvaṃ sādhyadharma utpattimattvādinā liṅgena niścitaṃ rāgādimattvaṃ tv aniścitam iti saṃdigdha
body.translated_text: is a correct example (<s>samyagdṛṣṭānta</s>). But that by which the twofold characteristic [of the reason] is not demonstrated is a fallacious example (<s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsa</s>) — thus it is stated. For instance: 'Sound is permanent, because of incorporeality, like action (<s>karma</s>)' — this is a fallacious example deficient in the property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharmavikala</s>). For in action, permanence — the property to be proved — does not exist, since action is impermanent. However, incorporeality — the proving property — does exist [in action]. [Another type:] deficient in the proving

body.text: sādhana
body.translated_text: property (<s>sādhanadharma</s>)

body.text: dharmā / asarvajño 'yaṃ puruṣo rāgādīmattvād rathyāpuruṣavat / saṃdigdhobhayadharmā / sādhyadharmasādhanadharmavyāvṛtter rathyāpuruṣe niścetum aśakyatvād anvayo / yatra sādhyena hetor vyāptir nāsti so 'nanvayaḥ / yo vaktā sa rāgādimān iṣṭapuruṣavat / atrānvayo nāsti / na hi rāgādīnāṃ vacanasya tādātmyalakṣaṇas tadutpattilakṣano vā pratibandho 'sti yenātrānvayaḥ
body.translated_text: . 'This person is not omniscient, because of having passions and so forth, like a man in the street' — [this has] doubtful both properties. Since the exclusion of both the property to be proved and the proving property cannot be ascertained with certainty regarding the man in the street, [this is] concordance (<s>anvaya</s>) [where]: wherever the concomitance of the reason with the property to be proved does not exist, that is non-concordance (<s>ananvaya</s>). 'Whoever is a speaker has passions and so forth, like a desired person' — here concordance is absent. For there is no identity-relation between passions and speaking.

body.text: syāt / apratidarśitānvayaḥ / yathānityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvād ghaṭavad / atra yady api kṛtakatvasyānityatvenānvayo 'sti / na tu vacanenākhyāta ity avidyamāna ivāsau / vyāpyavyāpakabhāvasya vacanenāpradarśitatvād iti / viparītānvayaḥ / yathā yad anityaṃ tat kṛtakam / atra hi yat kṛtakaṃ tad anityam ity anvaye vaktavye yad anityaṃ tat kṛtakam iti viparītam anvayaṃ karoti sarva ete dṛṣṭāntadoṣāḥ sādharmyeṇa //
body.translated_text: Non-demonstrated concordance (<s>apradarśitānvaya</s>): for example, 'Sound is impermanent, because of being produced, like a pot.' Here, although the concordance of being produced with impermanence exists, it has not been stated verbally — so it is as if non-existent, since the relation of pervaded and pervader has not been demonstrated by the statement. Reversed concordance (<s>viparītānvaya</s>): such as 'Whatever is impermanent is produced.' For here [the correct form should be] 'Whatever is produced is impermanent.'

body.text: 20. tathā vaidharmyeṇāpi / yathā nityaḥ śabdaḥ / amūrtatvāt / paramāṇuvad iti sādhyāvyatirekī / nityatvāt paramāṇoḥ sādhyaṃ na vyāvṛttam / atraiva karmavad iti dṛṣṭānte sādhanāvyatirekī / amūrtatvāt karmaṇaḥ / sādhanam atrāvyāvṛttam / ākāśavad iti kṛta ubhayāvyatirekī / ato hy ubhayaṃ na vyāvṛttaṃ / nityatvād amūrtatvād ākāśasya / tathā saṃdigdhasādhyavyatirekaḥ / yathā 'sarvajñāḥ kapilādayaḥ / avidyamānasarvajñatāliṅgabhūtapramāṇātiśayaśāsanatvāt / atra vaidharmyodāharaṇam / yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sa jyotirjñānādikam upadiṣṭavān / yathā vardhamānādiḥ / vardhamānāder asarvajñatāyāḥ sādhyadharmasya saṃdigdho ubhayavyatirekaḥ / saṃdigaha vyatirekaḥ /
body.translated_text: 20. Likewise through dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>) also: 'Sound is permanent, because of incorporeality, like an atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>)' — this lacks the exclusion of the property to be proved (<s>sādhyāvyatirekī</s>), since permanence — the property to be proved — is not excluded from the atom, as the atom is permanent. With the same [thesis but] 'like action' as the example — this lacks the exclusion of the proving property (<s>sādhanāvyatirekī</s>), since the proving property [incorporeality] is not excluded from action, as action is incorporeal. 'Like space (<s>ākāśa</s>)' — this makes [the example] lacking in the exclusion of both properties (<s>ubhayāvyatirekī</s>), since from space neither [property] is excluded.

body.text: saṃdigdhasādhanvyatirekaḥ
body.translated_text: Doubtful exclusion of the proving property (<s>saṃdigdhasādhanavyatireka</s>) —

body.text: yathā na trayīvidā brāhmaṇena grāhyavacanaḥ kaścid vivakṣitaḥ puruṣo rāgādimattvāt / atra vaidharmyodāharaṇam / ye grāhyavacanā na te rāgādimantas tad yathā gautamādayo dharmaśāstrāṇāṃ praṇetāraḥ / gautamādibhyo ragādimattvasya sādhanadharmasya vyāvṛttiḥ saṃdigdhā / saṃdigdhobhayavyatirekaḥ / yathāvītarāgāḥ kapilādayaḥ / parigrahāgrahayogāt / parigraho jīvitapariṣkārāṇaṃ svīkāraḥ / āgrahas teṣv
body.translated_text: for example: 'No intended person who possesses passions and so forth is one whose words should be accepted, like a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who knows the three <s>Vedas</s>.' Here the dissimilar example is: 'Those whose words should be accepted do not have passions and so forth — like <s>Gautama</s> and other authors of <s>dharmaśāstras</s> (legal treatises).' The exclusion of the proving property — possession of passions and so forth — from <s>Gautama</s> and others is doubtful. Doubtful exclusion of both properties (<s>saṃdigdhobhayavyatireka</s>) — as in

body.text: evābhiṣvaṅgaḥ / atra vaidharmyād udāharaṇam / yo vītarāgo na tasya parigrahāgrahau / yathā ṛṣabhādeḥ / ṛṣabhāder avītarāgatvaparigrahāgrahayoḥ sādhyasādhanadharmayor vyatirekaḥ saṃdigdhaḥ / avyatireko yathāvītarāgo vaktṛtvāt / yatra vītarāgatvaṃ nāsti na sa vaktā yathopalakhaṇḍa iti / yady api upalakhaṇḍād ubhayaṃ vyāvṛttaṃ / tathāpi sarvo vītarāgo na vakteti vyāptyā vyatirekāsiddher avyatirekaḥ / apradarśitavyatirekaḥ / yathānityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvād ākāśavad iti vaidharmyeṇa / yo hy anityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvād iti prayoge vaidharmyeṇākāśavad iti brūyāt tena vidyamāno 'pi vyatireko na pradarśitaḥ tathā / yadāśeṣapadārthopasaṃhāreṇānityatvābhāve kṛtakatvābhāvo yathākāśavad iti karoti tadā vyatireko darśito bhavati / na punar upamānamātreṇa / viparītavyatirekaḥ / yathā yad akṛtakaṃ tan nityam / atra hi yan nityaṃ tad akṛtakam iti vaktavye / yad akṛtakaṃ tan nityam iti vadati //
body.translated_text: the very same attachment [example]. Here the dissimilar example: 'One who is free from passion (<s>vītarāga</s>) does not have attachment or non-attachment [to possessions] — like <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and others.' The exclusion from <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and others of the two properties — non-freedom-from-passion and attachment/non-attachment — which are the properties to be proved and the proving property, is doubtful. Non-exclusion (<s>avyatireka</s>): 'one who is not free from passion, because of being a speaker.' 'Where freedom from passion does not exist, that one is not a speaker — like a stone slab.' body.text: 21. na hy ebhir dṛṣṭāntābhāsair hetoḥ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ sapakṣa eva sattvam asapakṣe cāsattvam eva niścayena śakyaṃ darśayituṃ viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ vā / ebhiḥ sādhyavikalair dṛṣṭāntābhāsair hetoḥ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ niścayena

children.translated_text: cannot

children.text: śakyaṃ darśayituṃ viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ veti saṃbandhanīyaṃ tadarthāpattyaiṣā
children.translated_text: be shown with certainty, nor the specific characteristic — this should be connected [with the above]. The refutation of these [fallacious examples] should be understood as [arising] by implication (<s>arthāpatti</s>) —
[of]

children.text: nirāso veditavyaḥ / yasmād ebhir dṛṣṭāntābhāsair dvividham api lakṣaṇaṃ na śakyaṃ darśayitum / tasmād arthāpattyaiṣāṃ nirāso draṣṭavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: that. Since by these fallacious examples the twofold characteristic cannot be demonstrated, therefore their refutation should be seen [as arising] by implication.

body.translated_text: 21. For by these fallacious examples, the general characteristic of the reason — its presence only in the similar case (<s>sapakṣa</s>) and its absence only in the dissimilar case (<s>asapakṣa</s>) — cannot be shown with certainty, nor the specific characteristic.

body.text: 22. dūṣaṇā nyūnatādyuktiḥ / dūṣyate 'nayeti dūṣaṇā /
body.translated_text: 22. Refutation (<s>dūṣaṇā</s>) is the reasoning of deficiency and the like. That by which [a thesis] is refuted is refutation.

body.text: ṇyāsaśrantho yuc / ādiśabdenāsiddhaviruddhānaikāntikāḥ / dṛṣṭāntadoṣāś ca gṛhyante ye pūrvaṃ nyūnatādayaḥ sādhanadoṣā uktās teṣām udbhāvanaṃ tena pareṣṭārthasiddhipratibandhāt / anena ca yad ahrīkeṇoktaṃ viparyayasādhanam eva dūṣaṇaṃ nānyad iti tad api parāstaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ / na hi viparyayasādhanād eva dūṣaṇaṃ / viruddhavat / api tu parasyābhipretaniścayapratibandhāt / niścayābhāvo vā bhavati niścayaviparyaya ity asty eva viparyayasiddhiḥ / dūṣaṇābhāsās tu jātayaḥ / abhūtadoṣodbhāvanāni jātyuttarāṇi / jātyā sadṛśyenottarāṇi / uttarasthānaprayuktatvād //
body.translated_text: [In the compound,] the affix 'yuc' [is applied]. By the word 'and so forth' (<s>ādiśabda</s>), the unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), and inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) [fallacies of the reason] are included, as well as the defects of the example. The faults of the proof previously stated as deficiency and so forth — their demonstration [constitutes refutation], since it obstructs the establishment of the opponent's intended meaning. By this, what has been said shamelessly — that 'refutation is only proving the opposite, nothing else' — that too should be seen as rejected. For [it is] not [just] from proving the opposite

body.text: iti tarkasopāne parārthānumānaparicchedas tṛtīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Tarkasopāna</s>, the third chapter on inference-for-others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>) [is concluded].

children.text: yat tarkasopānam idaṃ vidhāya puṇyaṃ mayāptaṃ śaradinduśubhram /
children.translated_text: Whatever merit I have obtained by composing this <s>Tarkasopāna</s> (Stairway of Reasoning), bright as the autumn moon —

children.text: tenottamāṃ bodhim ahaṃ labheya lokaś ca niryātu bhavād aśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: by that may I attain the supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), and may the entire world depart from [the cycle of] existence.

body.text: kṛtir iyaṃ paṇḍitavidyākaraśāntipādānām // //
body.translated_text: This is the work of the learned master <s>Vidyākaraśāntipāda</s>.
